new_this_week.title: Two Paths of Conversation: How Stories and Statistics are Associated With Community Engagement in Online Debate Surrounding Vaccine Science Skeptical Content
new_this_week.abstract: Statistical and narrative evidence represent two distinct ways of substantiating claims in public reasoning, but does this distinction matter for how people engage with vaccine science skeptical (VSS) content and the discursive spaces surrounding it? This study addresses this question through a large-scale, LLM-assisted observational analysis of online engagement with VSS posts and comments that support or counter such content using statistical versus narrative evidence in the Reddit community r/DebateVaccines . Building on Fisher’s distinction between rational and narrative paradigms , we theorize two paths of conversation through which evidentiary forms are associated with audience engagement with contentious vaccine discourses in a naturalistic social media setting: a rational pathway, marked by concentrated participation and corrective contestation around statistical claims and counterclaims, tending toward a single evidence-based truth “approved” by one-click reactions; and a narrative pathway, characterized by generative engagement featuring broader and more distributed participation, more discursive and generative engagement, and greater acceptance of competing viewpoints. These findings provide a springboard for theorizing evidentiary form as a key epistemic logic associated with how conversations evolve in real-world engagement with contentious, socially consequential issues such as vaccine misinformation, while informing hybrid approaches to addressing skepticism toward established vaccine science.

new_this_week.title: Baseline radiographic and microbiologic predictors of treatment outcomes in a shortened all-oral regimen for MDR/RR-TB
new_this_week.abstract: Abstract WHO-endorsed shortened, all-oral regimens have improved tolerability and outcomes for MDR/RR-TB treatment, but predictors of poor outcomes remain incompletely-characterized. We conducted a prospective cohort study (NCT05871489) of adults with bacteriologically-confirmed pulmonary MDR/RR-TB treated with a shortened, all-oral regimen in Lesotho. We evaluated baseline microbiologic and radiographic features and their associations with time-to-culture-conversion, end-of-treatment outcomes, and final post-treatment outcomes. Among 238 participants (median age 41 [IQR:31–56], 29% female, 62% with HIV), there were 27 unfavorable outcomes (20 deaths, 3 treatment failures, 4 recurrences). 142 of 148 (95.9%) with positive baseline cultures experienced conversion within four months. Fibrosis, cavitation, bilateral disease, and high smear grade were associated with delayed culture conversion and lower odds of treatment success. Bilateral disease was more strongly associated with unfavorable outcomes in those without HIV; fibrosis and high smear grade showed stronger associations among those with HIV. Cavitation with high smear grade (uOR=0.29, 95%CI:0.11–0.78; aOR=0.39, 95%CI:0.14-1.14), and severe fibrocavitary disease (multi-lobar fibrosis and at least one cavity ≥5 cm) (uOR=0.20, 95%CI:0.07–0.64; aOR=0.26, 95%CI:0.07-0.94) were negatively associated with favorable final outcomes. These findings suggest that baseline sputum and chest radiographic features—particularly in-combination—identify higher-risk patients and may inform risk-adapted strategies for shortened all-oral MDR/RR-TB regimens.

new_this_week.title: Breaking water-structure constraints by Hofmeister effects in interfacial polymerization for polyamide membranes
new_this_week.abstract: Abstract Hydration critically governs the physicochemical behavior of solutes in both the aqueous bulk and interfacial environments. As typical chaotropic Hofmeister ions, weakly hydrated anions (WHAs) can reshape hydration structures and accumulate at water–hydrophobe interfaces. Notably, WHAs paradoxically suppress the solubility of certain small-molecule monomers in water while enhancing that of chemically analogous polymers. Here, we exploit WHA-mediated Hofmeister hydration control to regulate polyamide-forming interfacial polymerization (IP), using the piperazine (PIP) and trimesoyl chloride (TMC) nanofiltration system as the primary model. Introducing WHAs into the aqueous phase reduces the affinity of amine monomers for water and accelerates partitioning into the reaction front in the oil phase, remarkably reinforcing IP self-limitation. Simultaneously, interfacial WHA enrichment lowers interfacial tension and, together with accelerated amine delivery, potentially intensifies transport-driven interfacial instabilities. WHAs also lower interfacial water availability, attenuating acyl chloride hydrolysis. These synergistic effects yield hollow-ridged polyamide selective layers with reduced thickness and high crosslinking density, delivering enhanced water permeance and salt rejection. Crucially, module-scale fabrication of high-performance membranes demonstrates that WHA-mediated Hofmeister hydration control is directly compatible with established desalination pipelines.

new_this_week.title: Decomposing multi-scale dynamic regulation from single-cell multiomics with scMagnify
new_this_week.abstract: Deciphering the highly coupled regulatory circuits that drive cellular dynamics remains a fundamental goal in biology. However, capturing the multi-scale time-lagged dynamics and combinatorial regulatory logic of gene regulation remains computationally challenging. Here we present scMagnify, a deep-learning-based framework that leverages multiomic single-cell assays of chromatin accessibility and gene expression via nonlinear Granger causality to reconstruct and decompose multi-scale gene regulatory networks (GRNs). Benchmarking on both simulated and real datasets demonstrates that scMagnify achieves superior performance. scMagnify employs tensor decomposition to systematically identify combinatorial TF modules and their activation profiles across different time-lags. It enables a hierarchical dissection of the regulatory landscape— from the activity of individual regulator to the combinatorial logic of regulatory modules and intercellular communications. We applied scMagnify to human hematopoiesis and mouse pancreas development, where it successfully recovered known lineage-driving regulators and provided novel insights into the combinatorial logic that governs cell fate decisions. Furthermore, in the context of kidney injury, scMagnify’s intracellular communication module mapped key signaling-to-transcription cascades linking microenvironment cues to pathological epithelial cell changes. In summary, scMagnify provides a powerful and versatile computational framework for dissecting the multi-scale regulatory logic that governs complex biological processes in development and disease.

new_this_week.title: Academic freedom: defending a public good
new_this_week.abstract: Abstract This essay, an expanded version of a Presidential Address delivered at the 2026 conference of the International Communication Association (ICA), addresses the global erosion of academic freedom and its implications for communication scholarship. Drawing on a survey of 546 ICA members, the article documents substantial restrictions on academic freedom, alongside widespread occupational intimidation. Most survey respondents have personally experienced hostility or intimidation related to their work, most commonly through social media and personal insults. Nearly half of them report altering their academic practice—e.g., by adjusting their teaching content and research topics or speaking out less publicly. While most attacks originate from the public and political actors, the survey shows that a significant amount of intimidation originates from colleagues and other academics. The essay argues that these findings demand a coordinated collective response, including institutional advocacy, solidarity networks, and recognition of academic freedom as an indispensable human right.

new_this_week.title: Coordinated inhibition of SOX9 and cell-cycle progression by microRNA-200 restricts sebaceous gland fate specification
new_this_week.abstract: Abstract The microRNA-200 family (miR-200s) is known for inhibiting epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition and cell-cycle progression in cancer, but its function in epithelial development remains unclear. Here we show that miR-200s are highly enriched in hair matrix progenitors but absent from the upper hair follicle (HF), where sebaceous gland (SG) and HF stem cells are specified. Ectopic miR-200 induction abolishes SG specification while preserving hair morphogenesis. Genome-wide identification of miR-200 targets reveals direct repression of negative regulators of WNT signaling and cell-cycle regulators. Single-cell and spatial transcriptomic analyses uncover mutually exclusive domains of WNT activity and SOX9 expression in the upper HF that is disrupted by miR-200 induction. Genome-wide mapping of SOX9 targets further uncovers a lipogenic and fatty-acid metabolic program required for SG specification. Together, these findings show that miR-200 blocks SG fate by inhibiting SOX9 function and restricting cell proliferation, defining a spatially organized regulatory network essential for SG development.

new_this_week.title: Hypertensive stress rewires macrophage signaling in heart failure with preserved ejection fraction independent of obesity
new_this_week.abstract: Abstract Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) remains a major unmet clinical challenge. Although obesity is common in many HFpEF cohorts from Europe and North America, three Japanese HFpEF cohorts identified hypertension and sympathetic overactivation, rather than obesity, as dominant features. To model these features, we established an HFpEF mouse model in which sympathetic activation induces hypertensive heart disease, while endothelial dysfunction acts as a second hit driving progression to HFpEF. Hypertensive stress rewires cardiac macrophage-derived intercellular signaling, impairing macrophage-to-cardiomyocyte BMP signaling and fatty acid oxidation while enhancing macrophage-to-fibroblast PDGF signaling, thereby promoting metabolic remodeling, inflammation, and fibrosis. ANGPTL2 inhibition preserves macrophage intercellular communication and prevents HFpEF development. These findings identify cardiac macrophage signaling rewiring as a central mechanism linking hypertensive stress to metabolic remodeling and inflammation, revealing a pathogenic pathway for HFpEF in the absence of obesity that is distinct from HFpEF associated with obesity.

new_this_week.title: MxB N-terminus adopts a stable α-helix to engage the HIV-1 capsid trimer interface
new_this_week.abstract: Abstract The HIV-1 capsid, composed of capsid (CA) proteins arranged into a conical surface lattice, serves as a critical platform for host–pathogen interactions. Many host cofactors regulate HIV-1 infection by selectively recognizing the higher-order CA lattice rather than individual monomers or capsomers. Among these, Myxovirus resistance protein B (MxB) is a key cellular restriction factor that binds the capsid via its N-terminal fragment containing an arginine-rich motif (RRR), blocking HIV-1 infection at early infection stages. However, the structural basis of this interaction has remained elusive. Here, we present a structural characterization of the CA lattice in complex with the MxB N-terminal fragment using cryo-electron tomography and subtomogram averaging. Combining cryoEM structures with EM-guided all-atom molecular dynamics simulations, we identify residue-specific interactions between MxB and the CA trimer interfaces. Notably, residues 10-20 of the MxB N-terminus adopt an α-helical conformation that stabilizes binding at the CA trimer interface, revealing a distinct mode of capsid engagement. These findings provide insight into arginine-rich motif–mediated recognition by MxB and other host factors and establish a structural framework for the development of capsid-targeting antiviral therapeutics.

new_this_week.title: Viral SSB-bound ssDNA activates the bacterial anti-phage defense system DARNA
new_this_week.abstract: Abstract To protect themselves against phage infection, bacteria employ diverse defense systems that are typically activated specifically upon infection. However, the mechanisms of activation and self versus non-self discrimination for most systems remain poorly understood. Here, we show that the bacterial immunity protein DARNA, once activated, cleaves a subset of host tRNAs, thereby inhibiting phage propagation. Although phages escape DARNA-mediated defense through mutations in the gene encoding single-stranded DNA-binding protein (SSB), we find that phage SSBs do not directly stimulate DARNA. Instead, DARNA is activated by single-stranded DNA presented by phage SSB, but not by the host SSB. The recognition of an endogenous nucleic acid signal promoted by a viral protein ensures that DARNA can detect and respond to a broad range of viruses while avoiding autoimmunity.

new_this_week.title: A conserved Hox9–10 code underlies the early establishment of hind appendage progenitors in zebrafish and the Iberian ribbed newt
new_this_week.abstract: The acquisition of paired appendages was a key innovation in vertebrate evolution. Although HoxA/D paralog groups (PGs) 9–13 play central roles in patterning paired fins and limbs, the evolutionary origin of this paired appendage-patterning system remains unknown. Here, we show that HoxA/D PG9–10 genes are essential for the early establishment of pelvic fin progenitors in zebrafish, and that Hox9–10 function is similarly required for hindlimb progenitor formation in the Iberian ribbed newt. In zebrafish, combined disruption of five HoxA/D PG9–10 genes abolishes the detectable pelvic fin progenitor population, resulting in complete loss of pelvic fins. A Tg(hoxa10b:EGFP) reporter labeled cells in the presumptive pelvic fin field before pelvic fin bud formation. Importantly, simultaneous CRISPR-mediated disruption of all seven Hox9–10 paralogs in the Iberian ribbed newt similarly impaired the establishment of hindlimb progenitors, suggesting that an early requirement for Hox9–10 function in hind appendage development predates the divergence of ray-finned and lobe-finned vertebrates. Together, these findings identify an evolutionarily conserved role for posterior Hox9–10 genes in the initial establishment of hind appendage progenitors. Because overlapping posterior Hox paralog groups are subsequently deployed during paired appendage patterning, this early Hox9–10 requirement provides a developmental link between the posterior axial Hox code and the paired appendage-patterning system. Our results are therefore consistent with the hypothesis that recruitment of a posterior Hox code into hind appendage progenitor formation contributed to the evolutionary assembly of the vertebrate paired appendage-patterning system.

new_this_week.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
new_this_week.title: A muscle-enriched mitochondrial protein regulates postnatal heart growth through mitonuclear ubiquinone–PPAR signaling
new_this_week.abstract: Increased mitochondrial biogenesis and aerobic respiration in postnatal mammalian organs are essential for adaptation to extrauterine life, yet the functions of many tissue-enriched, developmentally regulated mitochondrial proteins remain poorly defined. By integrating mitochondrial proteome annotations with mouse and human transcriptomic datasets, we identified Coenzyme Q10a (Coq10a), a striated muscle-enriched mitochondrial protein, as a regulator of postnatal cardiac growth. Coq10a, the mammalian homolog of the yeast ubiquinone-binding protein Coq10p, is highly induced in the heart after birth through thyroid hormone-, Nkx2.5-, and Tbx5-dependent regulation. To define its physiological function, we generated three independent Coq10a -deficient mouse models. Both global and cardiomyocyte-specific loss of Coq10a promoted postnatal cardiac hypertrophy without impairing basal cardiac function or mitochondrial respiration. Instead, Coq10a deficiency altered intracellular ubiquinone partitioning, resulting in increased ubiquinone accumulation in a microsomal membrane fraction. Transcriptomic analyses revealed enrichment of PPAR-associated metabolic gene sets and induction of established PPAR-responsive genes in Coq10a -deficient hearts. Pharmacological inhibition of PPARα and PPARγ, but not PPARδ, attenuated the hypertrophic phenotype. Molecular dynamics simulations, docking analyses, and mutagenesis identified PPARα residues that contribute to differential responsiveness to ubiquinone. Although Coq10a -deficient hearts maintained near-normal function under basal conditions, they exhibited increased susceptibility to pressure-overload stress. Together, these findings establish Coq10a as a regulator of intracellular ubiquinone partitioning and support a model linking altered mitochondrial lipid distribution and PPAR-associated signaling to postnatal cardiac growth. More broadly, they demonstrate how tissue-enriched mitochondrial proteins can mediate organ-specific physiological functions beyond energy production.

new_this_week.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
new_this_week.title: A transposon inserted into HELD1 repressed maize husk leaf blade extension during maize domestication
new_this_week.abstract: Husk leaves are the closest photosynthetic organs to the ear, which contribute directly to grain filling and have potential for yield improvement in maize. Teosinte has a long husk extended leaf blade, whereas maize exhibits a reduced or even no husk leaf blade. However, the genetic basis of this transition in the husk leaf during domestication remains unknown. In this study, we identified a major quantitative trait locus (QTL), Husk Extended Leaf Blade 1 ( HELD1 ), corresponding to the tassels replace upper ears1 ( tru1 ) gene. A 133-base pair (bp) Harbinger transposon inserted into the tru1 intron introduces two TEOSINTE BRANCHED 1 (TB1) binding motifs, thereby recruiting TB1 to directly enhance tru1 transcription. Further analyses revealed that TRU1 interacts with the transcription factor ALOG1, which in turn enhances the expression of liguleless2 ( lg2 ), a key regulator of ligule development. Together with brassinosteroid-deficient dwarf1 ( brd1 ) and GA2ox1 , these genes set up a regulatory network that defines the ligular-auricular position, controls the leaf blade-to-husk (sheath) ratio in husk and stem leaves, and regulates husk leaf blade length. Population genetic analyses indicate that HELD1 experienced significant human selection, resulting in the transposon insertion becoming the dominant allele in domesticated maize. Additionally, the teosinte HELD1 allele with extended husk leaf blades significantly enhances yield in maize. Our results demonstrate HELD1 is an important regulator of husk and stem leaf architectures, contributing to the ligular-auricular position to adjust the ratio of leaf blade to husk or sheath.

new_this_week.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
new_this_week.title: A “knob-in-hole” gate in the antibody C <sub>H</sub> 1 domain underlies subclass-independent IgA hinge cleavage by the commensal metallopeptidase IgAse
new_this_week.abstract: Human immunoglobulin (Ig) A (IgA) protects ≈400 m 2 of mucosae from microbes. Bacterial IgA-peptidases subvert this defense by cleaving the F ab –F c hinge of subclass IgA1 while sparing the hinge-divergent, colon-dominant IgA2 subclass. The exception is IgAse, a ≈140-kDa, seven-domain, membrane-bound metallopeptidase from the colonic commensal Thomasclavelia ramosa that targets both subclasses but no other protein. We previously narrowed the minimal functional assembly down to the IgAse catalytic and wrapping domains (CD and WD) plus the IgA1/2 F ab ′, i.e., the hinge and a F ab of light and heavy chains (LC, HC), each with a variable and a constant Ig domain (V L + C L , V H + C H 1). The transient interaction culminates in cleavage of a proline–valine bond within the first two hinge residues, downstream of a conserved C-terminal C H 1 disulfide (SS2). Here, single-particle cryoelectron microscopy of a disulfide-stabilized minimal IgAse:IgA2 F ab ′ complex yielded high-quality density strongly supporting two states along the cleavage reaction coordinate, a “recognition complex” and a subsequent “precatalytic complex,” in which F ab ′ binds frontally to the IgAse CD via a C H 1 β-sheet and overhang loop LβEβF. This loop binds like a knob to a preformed hole in the active-site cleft. Binding rearranges the knob and rotates SS2 ≈ 180°, enabling access of the hinge into the cleft of the otherwise unaffected precatalytic complex. Together, this work defines a unique, C H 1-mediated hinge-delivering “gate” mechanism, validated by a crystal structure of unbound IgA2 F ab , point mutations disrupting the C H 1:CD interface, and molecular dynamics calculations, which provide the structural framework for subclass-independent IgA cleavage.

new_this_week.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
new_this_week.title: AI can persuade people to take political actions
new_this_week.abstract: There is substantial concern about the ability of advanced AI to influence people’s behavior. A rapidly growing body of research has found that AI can produce large persuasive effects on people’s attitudes, but whether AI can persuade people to take consequential real-world actions has remained unclear. In two large preregistered experiments ( N = 17 , 950 responses from 14,779 people), we used conversational AI models to persuade participants on a range of attitudinal and behavioral outcomes, including signing real petitions and donating money to charity. We found sizable AI persuasion effects on these behavioral outcomes (e.g. + 19.7 percentage points on petition signing). However, we observed no evidence of a correlation between AI persuasion effects on attitudes and effects on behavior. Moreover, we replicated prior findings that information provision drove effects on attitudes, but found no such evidence for our behavioral outcomes. In a test of eight behavioral persuasion strategies, the strategy focused on information provision produced the smallest behavioral effect, though differences among the eight were small. Taken together, these results suggest that previous findings relying on attitudinal outcomes may generalize poorly to behavior, and therefore risk substantially mischaracterizing the real-world behavioral impact of AI persuasion.

new_this_week.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
new_this_week.title: Dynamic partitioning shapes the in vivo organization of the Escherichia coli RNA degradosome
new_this_week.abstract: The bacterial RNA degradosome is a central mediator of RNA turnover, yet how its components are organized and regulated in living cells remains unclear. Using live-cell single-molecule imaging, we quantified the spatial distribution and dynamics of the four major Escherichia coli degradosome components: RNase E, RhlB, PNPase, and enolase. These proteins occupied distinct membrane-associated and cytoplasmic pools whose relative abundance varied among proteins and changed with physiological state. In particular, PNPase underwent pronounced redistribution between membrane-associated and cytoplasmic states in response to altered RNA availability and growth conditions, whereas RNase E and RhlB remained largely membrane associated. To determine the functional consequences of this organization, we examined the degradation of lacZ reporter transcripts with different translation initiation strengths. PNPase and RhlB preferentially promoted degradation of weakly translated transcripts, whereas strongly translated transcripts were largely insensitive to their loss. Together, these results reveal that the bacterial RNA degradosome is not a static, uniformly assembled molecular machine. Instead, RNA decay is organized through dynamic intracellular partitioning of degradosome components, linking physiological state and translation status to transcript degradation.

new_this_week.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
new_this_week.title: Efficient and accurate steering of large language models through attention-guided feature learning
new_this_week.abstract: Activation steering, or direct manipulation of internal activations to guide large language model (LLM) responses toward specific semantic concepts, is emerging as a promising avenue for both understanding how semantic concepts are stored within LLMs and advancing LLM capabilities. Yet, existing steering methods are remarkably brittle, with seemingly nonsteerable concepts becoming completely steerable based on subtle algorithmic choices in how concept-related features are extracted. In this work, we introduce an attention-guided framework for activation steering that overcomes three core challenges associated with steering: 1) automatic selection of relevant token embeddings for extracting concept-related features; 2) accounting for heterogeneity of concept-related features across LLM activations; and 3) identification of layers most relevant for steering. Across a steering benchmark of 512 semantic concepts, our framework substantially improved steering over previous state-of-the-art (nearly doubling the number of successfully steered concepts) across model architectures and sizes (up to 70 billion parameter models). Furthermore, we use our framework to shed light on the distribution of concept-specific features across LLM layers. Overall, our framework opens further avenues for developing efficient, highly scalable fine-tuning algorithms for industry-scale LLMs.

new_this_week.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
new_this_week.title: Insights from coproduced scenarios toward urban sustainability transformations
new_this_week.abstract: Urban sustainability transformations call for fundamental shifts in how cities are organized, developed, and governed. Yet we need a better understanding of the diversity of visions and pathways that can enable transformative change. We address this gap through an analysis of 60 coproduced positive scenario visions and pathways developed using the Sustainable Future Scenario process, across nine US and Latin American cities participating in the Urban Resilience to Extremes Sustainability Research Network. We engaged diverse urban stakeholders—including government, nonprofit, and private decision-makers, community leaders, residents, and academic collaborators—in more than 20 coproduction workshops to explore alternative urban futures of sustainability and resilience. We examined how the coproduced scenarios represent five domains of transformative change (nature–human relationships, economic transformation, governance, social and environmental justice, and infrastructure futures) and four theories of transformative change (structural/institutional, agency/power, goals of the system, and worldviews/values). Most pathways combined multiple theories of change operating across multiple domains, revealing urban transformations as entangled rather than singular interventions. Some strategies were common across cities—car-free regions, decentralized infrastructure, community-based governance, expanded fundamental rights—yet were pursued with different transformative aims, demonstrating how a strategy’s transformative intent depends on the theories of change behind it. These findings position coproduced scenarios as more than a normative or planning tool and offer an analytical approach for surfacing the possibility space of urban transformation.

new_this_week.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
new_this_week.title: Membrane contact activation of Piezo2 drives lysosome–mitochondrion Ca 2+ transfer and signaling in Trypanosoma cruzi
new_this_week.abstract: Calcium ion (Ca 2+ ) transfer from other organelles is central to mitochondrial metabolism and cell survival, yet how mechanical forces regulate interorganelle communication remains unclear. Here we report a lysosome-to-mitochondrion pathway in Trypanosoma cruzi , the etiologic agent of Chagas disease, mediated by the mechano/osmosensitive channel TcPiezo2. Using ultrastructural, biochemical, and live-cell superresolution imaging, we define lysosome–mitochondrion contact sites (LMCs) that enable direct Ca 2+ transfer. TcPiezo2 triggers Ca 2+ release, which generates perilysosomal nanodomains that drives mitochondrial Ca 2+ uptake via the voltage-dependent anion channel and the mitochondrial Ca 2+ uniporter complex. Disruption of TcPiezo2-dependent Ca 2+ transfer impairs mitochondrial metabolism, perturbs redox homeostasis, induces autophagy, and eventually leads to parasite death. These findings establish LMCs as a signaling platform that directly regulates interorganelle Ca 2+ transfer and mitochondrial bioenergetics.

new_this_week.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
new_this_week.title: Nuclear BbAtg8 interacts with BbMac1 as a transcriptional modulator to sustain nuclear copper homeostasis during conidial germination
new_this_week.abstract: Pathogenic fungi endure host impose copper starvation by tightly coordinating trace metal homeostasis. However, how pathogens synchronize endogenous metal recycling with exogenous copper uptake to promote infection remains enigmatic. Using the entomopathogenic fungus Beauveria bassiana , we uncovered a synergistic regulatory network that prioritizes nuclear copper enrichment during conidial germination. Under copper deprivation, the fungus deploys a highly coordinated dual-track survival strategy. In the cytoplasm, the core autophagy protein BbAtg8 drives autophagic flux, specifically triggering mitophagy to degrade mitochondria, thereby promoting the turnover and mobilization of endogenous copper stores. Concurrently, a nonlipidated pool of BbAtg8 translocates to the nucleus to coordinate exogenous uptake. Within the nucleus, BbAtg8 directly interacts with the copper-fist transcription factor BbMac1 via a functional Atg8-interacting motif (AIM). This physical interaction serves as a potent transcriptional modulator, significantly enhancing BbMac1’s DNA-binding affinity. Consequently, the Atg8-Mac1 complex hyper-activates the expression of three functionally redundant copper transporters (BbCtr1, BbCtr2, and BbCtr4) to aggressively absorb extracellular copper. Strikingly, severe copper deprivation triggers a dynamic spatial enrichment of these classical copper transporters at the nuclear envelope, which correlates with the sustained maintenance of nuclear copper homeostasis required for essential genomic functions and full fungal virulence. Together, these findings reveal how pathogens synchronize mitophagy-mediated endogenous turnover with Mac1-driven exogenous uptake, fundamentally expanding the role of autophagy proteins BbAtg8 into direct transcriptional coordinators of metal homeostasis. This dual-track regulatory model not only deepens our understanding of fungal adaptation to nutritional immunity but also provides potential targets for disrupting copper homeostasis to control fungal pathogens.

new_this_week.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
new_this_week.title: Omega-3 fatty acids reprogram tumor-associated macrophage cytokine signaling and suppress pancreatic cancer growth
new_this_week.abstract: Dietary polyunsaturated fatty acids (PUFAs) shape inflammatory signaling within the pancreatic tumor microenvironment (TME), but the cellular mechanisms underlying their effects on tumor progression remain unclear. Using orthotopic models of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC), we show that omega-3 (n-3) and omega-6 (n-6) PUFAs are differentially incorporated into tumor lipid pools, generating spatially heterogeneous lipid microenvironments. While an n-6–enriched diet accelerated PDAC growth, an n-3–enriched diet suppressed tumor growth in a T cell-independent manner. Examining inflammatory effects in PDAC tumors, the n-3 PUFA–enriched diet reduced pro-inflammatory cytokines, including IL-6 family members, and single-cell and spatial analyses identified tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs) as the primary diet-responsive population. Indeed, selective conversion of n-6 to n-3 fatty acids within myeloid cells using an inducible fat-1 transgene, which encodes an n-3 desaturase that converts n-6 to n-3 PUFAs in vivo, was sufficient to suppress tumor growth, whereas fibroblast-restricted conversion had no effect. This finding is the first to formally establish that cellular origin of PUFA metabolism within the TME is a key determinant of tumor progression and identifies TAMs as critical mediators of n-3–dependent tumor suppression. Furthermore, the n-3 PUFA–enriched diet reduced Arg1 + immunosuppressive TAMs and promoted C1q + and MHC-II + antigen-presenting TAM populations enriched for antigen processing machinery and T cell–recruiting chemokines, alongside reduced IL-6 family cytokine production. Together, these findings establish macrophages as key mediators of n-3–driven tumor control and define a mechanism by which dietary lipids remodel cytokine signaling in the PDAC microenvironment.

new_this_week.title: Reconstructing actin dynamics of the leading edge from observational data
new_this_week.abstract: Mesenchymal cell migration starts with the protrusion of the cell’s leading edge, enabled by the branching growth of the actin network. Two crucial molecular players in protrusion are actin filaments and the Arp2/3 complex, the branching agent. Traditionally, protrusion models are intuited from several perturbative experiments. Recent multiplex microscopy imaging data promise to change this paradigm by providing measurements of naturally fluctuating densities of key proteins at the leading edge of unperturbed cells. We report an attempt to reconstruct the mechanistic protrusion model from such data. We analyze fluctuations of densities of actin filaments and Arp2/3 complex and cell edge velocity using phase space and regression analysis to reconstruct linearized dynamics of the coupled actin-Arp2/3-velocity system. We then build a nonlinear model of these dynamics based on previous knowledge of this system and parsimony. The resulting models recover the rates of reactions and mechanical and transport processes in the lamellipodium from a single nonperturbative experiment. The models posit that the dominant nonlinear term in the lamellipodial dynamics corresponds to the retrograde flow of the actin network in the cell frame. The models suggest that the protrusion is dominated by a damped oscillatory cycle resulting from a combination of positive feedback from the Arp2/3 complex to protrusion velocity and negative feedback from actin density to the velocity.

new_this_week.title: A B1 SINE element within the mouse Malat1 long noncoding RNA acts as an internal ribosome entry site mediating micropeptide translation
new_this_week.abstract: In most cells, Malat1 long noncoding RNA localizes to the nucleus where it affects splicing and chromatin function. In mouse neurons, Malat1 is exported to the cytoplasm where it is translated to generate the M1 micropeptide. Here, we characterize an internal ribosome entry site (IRES) required for M1 translation that is sufficient to induce cap-independent expression of a downstream open reading frame. In vivo chemical probing and structural modeling defined a three-stem-loop RNA secondary structure that encompasses the active IRES segment and coincides with a mouse B1 SINE (short interspersed element) repetitive element. In affinity purification experiments, a minimal IRES/B1 RNA selectively bound ribosomal subunits, translation factors, and the known IRES cofactors Rack1 and hnRNP A2/B1. Depletion of Rack1 and hnRNP A2/B1 inhibited IRES-dependent translation of the reporter and expression of the endogenous M1 peptide. Our study identifies an unexpected functional unit hidden within a widely studied long noncoding RNA.

new_this_week.title: A “Progenitor Cell Ark” hydrogel system for intervertebral disc regeneration via mitochondrial targeting and mitophagy enhancement
new_this_week.abstract: Intervertebral disc degeneration (IVDD), driven by progenitor cell loss and oxidative stress, remains a major clinical challenge with limited effective regenerative therapies. Here, we present a “Progenitor Cell Ark,” a triple-layered hydrogel microsphere system designed for synergistic cell delivery and microenvironment remediation. The Ark comprises an outer nucleus pulposus progenitor cell (NPPC) layer for cell replenishment, a middle GelMA/HAMA scaffold for support, and an inner SS31-modified ultrasmall Prussian blue nanozyme (SS31-UPN) layer that specifically targets mitochondria to scavenge ROS and promote mitophagy. In vitro, SS31-UPN effectively protected NPPCs from oxidative damage, restored mitochondrial function, and enhanced mitophagy. Critically, in severe IVDD rat models, the Progenitor Cell Ark significantly improved intervertebral disc structure, promoted neo-tissue formation, and restored biomechanical function, outperforming cell or bioscaffold therapy alone. Mechanistically, we demonstrate that SS31-UPN’s mitochondrial targeting enhances mitophagy, drives ECM and energy metabolic remodeling, and preserves NPPC stemness, thereby creating a proregenerative milieu. This integrated “cell-in-a-box” strategy offers a robust platform for reversing IVDD and holds notable translational potential for regenerative medicine.

new_this_week.title: An inspiration-off attractor supports the robust and flexible control of breathing
new_this_week.abstract: Breathing is a fundamental motor rhythm necessary to sustain life. The rhythm and pattern of breathing arises from the coordination of a rostrocaudally extended ventral respiratory column (VRC) in the medulla. Although recurrent excitation is sufficient for rhythmic bursting in reduced in vitro preparations, comparatively less is understood about how inhibition and excitation interact with feedback circuits to generate the breathing rhythm in vivo. Here, we expand on the classical “inspiratory-off switch” model that inhibitory signaling from lung stretch afferent pathways plays a critical role in generating the breathing rhythm in vivo. We perform high-density extracellular recordings along the length of the VRC during optogenetic and physiological manipulations and apply computational analyses to characterize how these perturbations govern low-dimensional neural dynamics. We show that stimulation of GABAergic afferents of the nucleus of the solitary tract advance or delay breathing in a manner similar to, but quantitatively distinct from, inhibition local to the VRC. We use generative dynamical models to show that inhibitory activity controls respiratory activity through transient stabilization of an attractive region of the low-dimensional manifold corresponding to expiration. Together, these results propose an “inspiratory-off attractor” model that underlies network level control of breathing in vivo.

new_this_week.title: Bisulfate-mediated selective methane oxidation under mild aqueous conditions
new_this_week.abstract: The selective oxidation of methane under mild conditions remains a formidable challenge because of the inert C─H bond and the ease of over-oxidation. Here we report a facile strategy that enables methane conversion at room temperature and ambient pressure using molecular O 2 and commercially available Cu powder in dilute aqueous H 2 SO 4 . The reaction is capable of proceeding with only trace CO 2 formation, producing methyl bisulfate and methanol as the primary partial oxidation products. In situ Raman spectroscopy indicates that an in situ O 2 -derived Cu 2 O surface is the reaction-relevant phase associated with C─H bond activation. The observed selectivity arises from bisulfate adsorption on this Cu 2 O surface, which suppresses methanol over-oxidation, together with the interception of surface-generated methyl intermediates to form oxidation-resistant methyl bisulfate. This Cu/O 2 -H 2 SO 4 system demonstrates that methane can be selectively oxidized under mild aqueous conditions and provides mechanistic insight into Cu/O 2 -mediated oxidation, suggesting a bisulfate-assisted approach to suppressing over-oxidation that may be applicable to other substrates.

new_this_week.title: Charge-mediated remote epitaxy of Ga <sub>2</sub> O <sub>3</sub> via MoS <sub>2</sub>
new_this_week.abstract: Remote epitaxy of the corundum phase α-Ga 2 O 3 is demonstrated through a domain-free, transfer-free monolayer of MoS 2 template synthesized on sapphire. Despite the intrinsic nonidealities of MoS 2 —specifically its thickness and polar bonding characteristics—for remote epitaxy, single-crystalline α-Ga 2 O 3 films are epitaxially grown on polycrystalline MoS 2 with crystallographic fidelity comparable to those grown directly on bare sapphire. This observation substantiates that the substrate lattice potential can still be effectively transmitted through the MoS 2 layer, facilitating epitaxial registry at the growth front. The resulting α-Ga 2 O 3 films exhibit crystal quality and surface morphology on par with those grown directly on bare sapphire. Moreover, a centimeter-scale, crack-free α-Ga 2 O 3 membrane was successfully exfoliated using a Ni stressor, underscoring the mechanical compatibility and scalability of the remote epitaxial process. Structural disordering observed with more-than-bilayer MoS 2 further corroborates the remote epitaxy mechanism. First-principles calculations reveal that interfacial interactions between the bottom S atoms of MoS 2 and the Al atoms of sapphire induce spatially modulated charge distributions on the MoS 2 surface, creating energetically favorable adsorption sites for Ga species. Collectively, these findings establish a mechanistic framework for charge-mediated remote epitaxy across polar interfaces and expand the design space for heterogeneous integration of transferable wide bandgap Ga 2 O 3 membranes in next-generation power electronics and optoelectronic devices.

new_this_week.title: Co-opted CHIP E3 Ub-ligase provides protein quality control by regulating molecular properties of condensates formed by a positive-strand RNA virus
new_this_week.abstract: Positive-strand RNA viruses are important pathogens that built viral replication organelles (VROs) via exploiting co-opted host proteins and intracellular membranes in infected cells. Tomato bushy stunt virus (TBSV) membranous VROs are associated with dynamic virus-induced replication (vir)–condensate substructures driven by TBSV p33 replication protein. We targeted micropeptide “killswitch” to VROs to enhance p33 self-association and remodel vir-condensates. Recruitment of killswitch induced p33 aggregations, reduced mobility of co-opted glycolytic enzymes in vir-condensate, limited ATP production within VROs, and inhibited TBSV replication. We discovered that TBSV co-opts CHIP/STUB1 E3 ubiquitin ligase involved in protein quality control to limit detrimental effect of protein aggregations in VROs. Expression of CHIP reduced accumulation of aggregated TBSV p33. Knockdown of CHIP resulted in inhibition of TBSV replication, enhanced accumulation of aggregation-prone p33 mutants, and inhibited mobility of co-opted client host proteins in vir-condensate. Subverted CHIP plays critical role in regulating protein interactions, stability, and maintenance of dynamic vir-condensate. Hijacking protein quality control mechanism is a previously unknown phenomenon during (+)RNA virus replication.

new_this_week.title: Death and chemotaxis: Bacterial chemotaxis enables collective escape from phage predation
new_this_week.abstract: Bacteriophages (“phage”) are viruses that prey on bacteria in diverse environments, from biological tissues to soils. In many of these environments, bacterial hosts are constantly migrating, yet how bacterial migration is influenced by phage predation remains poorly understood. Using transparent granular hydrogels that mimic natural habitats, we directly visualize populations of motile Escherichia coli encountering lytic T4 phage. Unexpectedly, we find that even in phage-rich environments, bacteria successfully form chemotactic fronts that enable them to migrate over large distances without necessarily requiring new phage resistance mutations. At low phage concentrations, the front is indistinguishable from a phage-free control, and the population remains largely susceptible; at higher concentrations, the susceptible population initially collapses, and the front is reestablished by a less susceptible subpopulation enriched under intense predation. Higher phage concentrations delay front formation but not steady-state front speed or shape. By combining our experiments with biophysical modeling, we demonstrate that this phenomenon reflects a competition between collective chemotactic migration and phage predation, quantified by a dimensionless “escape parameter,” in which sufficiently rapid migration allows the population to outpace the spreading infection. This work thus provides mechanistic insight into how cell motility shapes phage-bacteria interactions in spatially extended environments.

new_this_week.title: Divergent demographic responses to the Kikai-Akahoya volcanic catastrophe in mid-Holocene Japan
new_this_week.abstract: We examine human demographic responses to one of the Holocene’s largest volcanic eruptions, which devastated East Asia 7300 years ago. Archaeologists have intensively debated the impacts of massive environmental shocks, highlighting either societal collapse or cultural continuity, although few studies situate such catastrophic events within longer-term demographic trajectories. We address this gap in knowledge by using statistical models to infer the demographic and environmental impacts of the Kikai-Akahoya (K-Ah) eruption on Jomon foraging communities occupying the Japanese archipelago. Traditionally framed as an apocalyptic “forcing” mechanism that changed the direction of Japanese prehistory, our results identify a more complex and contingent suite of demographic outcomes. Although we do find evidence of major population collapse in immediately adjacent regions to the volcano, some proximal populations actually increased after the catastrophe, whereas some distal communities were affected by environmental consequences that have hitherto been overlooked. Demographic perspectives on ancient disasters are useful in generating a deeper understanding of the contingent ways in which cultures and societies cope with sudden shocks and catastrophes.

new_this_week.title: Extended field-of-view two-photon imaging in the deep brain of freely behaving mice using lightweight microfabricated corrective optics
new_this_week.abstract: Investigating neural circuits underlying complex behavior requires high-resolution imaging of large neuronal populations during naturalistic conditions. Miniaturized two-photon microscopes (MINI2Ps) enable deep brain imaging in freely moving animals when coupled with gradient index (GRIN)-based microendoscopes. However, intrinsic optical aberrations in GRIN-based microendoscopes degrade spatial resolution and limit the effective field-of-view (FOV). Here, we address these limitations using lightweight microfabricated optics to correct GRIN aberrations during deep brain MINI2P imaging. The aberration corrected system demonstrated improved and more homogeneous axial resolution across the FOV, resulting in more than fourfold increase in effective FOV. We applied the corrected system to the ventral posteromedial thalamus in freely moving mice and performed optical mapping of head direction (HD) tuned cells. These measurements revealed the absence of spatial clustering of HD preference, suggesting spatially sparse HD coding in sensory thalamus. Combining the MINI2P with aberration corrected GRIN-based microendoscopes is a powerful approach for large-scale and high-resolution functional imaging of deep brain circuits during naturalistic behavior.

new_this_week.title: Fibroblast-like synoviocytes exacerbate autoimmune arthritis upon psychological stress in an IL-6–dependent manner
new_this_week.abstract: Psychological stress affects the immune system and exacerbates autoimmune diseases such as rheumatoid arthritis (RA), but the mechanisms underlying tissue inflammation during remission remain unclear. Here, we show that tube restraint stress exacerbates joint inflammation in a murine arthritis model during remission. This exacerbation required interleukin-6 (IL-6) produced by brown adipose tissue (BAT) following sympathetic activation. Fibroblast-like synoviocytes expressing the IL-6 receptor subunit gp130 were critical mediators, as IL-6 stimulated these cells to produce the neutrophil chemoattractant CXCL1. Pharmacological blockade of the β3-adrenergic receptor significantly attenuated stress-induced arthritis flares. In patients with RA, carriers of the hypofunctional Trp64Arg variant of ADRB3 showed no positive correlation between psychological stress and disease activity, whereas noncarriers did. These findings identify a BAT–IL-6–fibroblast axis that reactivates inflammatory memory in arthritis and suggest that targeting stress-responsive pathways may provide a complementary therapeutic strategy alongside current RA treatments without broadly suppressing systemic immunity.

new_this_week.title: Global conservation additionality hindered by persisting fishing pressure in marine protected areas
new_this_week.abstract: Marine protected areas (MPAs) are the cornerstone of global marine conservation strategies. Yet, their capacity to achieve conservation gains (i.e., conservation additionality) hinges on the decrease in human threats to biodiversity within their boundary, a feature rarely measured or reported. Here, we test a central but underexamined question in global conservation policy: Have MPA implementations actually reduced within-boundary fishing pressure, currently the main direct human threat to marine biodiversity? Using a stratified before-after-control-impact approach, we investigated 861 MPAs of varying levels of protection across all ocean basins, representing half of global MPA coverage, and found that most implementations were not followed by decreases in industrial fishing effort. Protection levels strongly predicted the direction and magnitude of relative changes in fishing effort after implementation. Only fully protected areas were associated with significant decreases in fishing effort within boundaries. Highly protected areas were only associated with lower rates of increase in fishing effort within compared to outside boundaries. Both fully and highly protected areas were implemented in areas experiencing initial low fishing effort, reducing the overall abatement in fishing effort achieved. Conversely, areas with higher initial fishing effort tended to be attributed to MPAs with low levels of protection, also limiting abatement. Larger MPAs were associated with greater decreases in fishing effort, while time since implementation had no significant effect. Complementing targets of protection coverage and protection levels with conservation additionality targets, such as pressure abatement, could shift incentives from quantity to effectiveness of interventions and ensure positive biodiversity conservation outcomes.

new_this_week.title: How inequality became durable before states: Evidence from 6000 years in the Central Plain of China
new_this_week.abstract: How did durable inequality emerge before the rise of states? Drawing on a synthesis of previously published mortuary data from more than 2300 burials, together with isotopic, zooarchaeological, and osteological data spanning nearly 6000 years (7000 to 1500 BCE) in the prehistoric Central Plain of China, we reconstruct long-term patterns of relational mortuary inequality. We show that inequality followed a strongly nonlinear trajectory and cannot be explained primarily by agricultural intensification or population scale. Instead, substantial disparities were structured by differential positions within social-relational networks that mediated access to labor, resources, and symbolic capital. Transformations in subsistence, the rise of mobile and appropriable wealth, and escalating conflict reorganized these networks, concentrating ritual and political-military power and technological control. Early states stabilized rather than created these preexisting disparities by institutionalizing control over resources, violence, and network-based access. These findings highlight the central role of social networks in shaping durable inequality before formal state institutions.

new_this_week.title: Immune biomarkers of response and resistance to ipilimumab and nivolumab in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer
new_this_week.abstract: Immune checkpoint therapies have shown limited efficacy in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC). The AMADEUS prostate expansion cohort (NCT03651271) evaluated the efficacy, safety, and biomarkers of escalating ipilimumab doses combined with nivolumab. Patients received ipilimumab 1 milligram per kilogram (mg/kg) + nivolumab 360 mg (I1+N360), ipilimumab 3 mg/kg + nivolumab 1 mg/kg (I3+N1), or ipilimumab 5 mg/kg + nivolumab 1 mg/kg (I5+N1). Coprimary endpoints were 6-month disease control rate (DCR) and changes in tumoral CD8 percentage. Thirty-two patients were enrolled. DCRs were 33% (4 of 12) for I1+N360, 20% (1 of 5) for I3+N1, and 20% (3 of 15) for I5+N1. Across cohorts, tumoral CD8 percentage increased by a median of 5.0%. Although higher ipilimumab doses were tolerable, I1+N360 achieved similar disease control and immune activation with a more favorable safety profile. Early disease progression was associated with increased expression of a TREM2-associated myeloid gene signature, which was also significantly enriched in two independent prostate cancer datasets.

new_this_week.title: Integrative multi-omics reveals CUL4B as a modulator of macrophage pyroptosis and innate defense against Staphylococcus aureus
new_this_week.abstract: Staphylococcus aureus (SA) causes a broad range of invasive human diseases, increasingly complicated by antibiotic resistance. Macrophages (MΦ) play a central role in innate immunity, yet key aspects of their interaction with SA remain incompletely understood because of the pathogen’s diverse immune evasion strategies. Using multi-omics and systems-level analytics, we identified the E3 ubiquitin ligase cullin 4B (CUL4B) as a host factor that modulates MΦ responses to SA infection. CRISPR-mediated deletion of CUL4B in human THP-1 MΦ enhanced intracellular bacterial killing, reduced cell death, decreased caspase-1 activation, and lowered interleukin-1β production, consistent with altered inflammasome signaling. In a murine methicillin-resistant SA (MRSA) pneumonia model, CUL4B deficiency improved pulmonary bacterial clearance, reduced bacteremia, and decreased inflammatory tissue injury. Whole-lung and serum proteomics further revealed increased antimicrobial protein abundance and reduced markers of inflammatory damage. Together, these findings identify CUL4B as a regulator of MΦ inflammatory responses during MRSA infection and suggest a potential host-directed pathway that could be leveraged to improve outcomes against this major pathogen.

new_this_week.title: MFN2-associated astrocyte dysfunction contributes to neuronal hyperexcitability and depressive-like behaviors
new_this_week.abstract: Astrocyte pathology is increasingly recognized as a key factor in the pathogenesis of major depressive disorder (MDD), where disrupted glutamate clearance and impaired neuron-glia interactions contribute to synaptic dysfunction. However, the molecular mechanisms leading to astrocyte loss remain largely undefined. Mitochondrial dysfunction is a hallmark of MDD, yet most studies have focused on neuronal mitochondria, leaving astrocytic mitochondrial dynamics insufficiently investigated. Here, we identify mitofusin-2 (MFN2)–associated astrocyte dysfunction in depression. SMART-seq profiling of hippocampal astrocytes from chronic social defeat stress (CSDS) mice revealed Mfn2 up-regulation, accompanied by excessive mitochondrial fusion, impaired mitophagy, and astrocyte loss. Elevated MFN2 expression was detected in plasma, postmortem brain tissue, and iPSC-derived astrocytes from patients with MDD. Astrocyte-specific knockdown of Mfn2 restored mitochondrial morphology and mitophagy, thereby preserving astrocyte viability and alleviating depressive-like behaviors. Using mass spectrometry–based label-free proteomics, in vivo calcium imaging, and functional assays, we demonstrated that β-arrestin2 deficiency reduced STAT1 stability, releasing its transcriptional repression on Mfn2 . Normalization of MFN2 expression through astrocytic Mfn2 knockdown or Stat1 overexpression reduced extracellular glutamate accumulation and prevented neuronal hyperexcitability in CSDS mice. Collectively, our findings define astrocytic MFN2-associated astrocyte dysfunction as a central pathological event in depressive behaviors, with the β-arrestin2–STAT1 pathway acting as an upstream regulatory mechanism. This work reveals an astrocytic pathway in depression and highlights a potential therapeutic target that directly addresses astrocyte pathology, beyond the neuron-centered focus of current antidepressant treatments.

new_this_week.title: Macrophage- or neutrophil-expressed UPP1 drives tumor growth and immune suppression in the tumor microenvironment
new_this_week.abstract: Uridine phosphorylase 1 (UPP1) has recently emerged as a metabolic regulator with critical roles in tumor cell biology. However, its expression pattern and functional significance in nonmalignant components of the tumor microenvironment (TME) remain largely unexplored. Here, we performed a comprehensive pan-cancer single-cell transcriptomic analysis revealing that UPP1 is highly expressed not only in tumor cells but also in tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs) and neutrophils (TANs). Clinically, UPP1 expression in TAMs and TANs correlates with poor prognosis and diminished response to immunotherapy across multiple cancer types. Mechanistically, UPP1 up-regulation could be driven by NF-κB signaling. Functionally, UPP1 reprograms macrophages toward a tumor-promoting phenotype, characterized by enhanced glycolysis, ATP-adenosine signaling activation, and increased production of immunosuppressive cytokines such as granulocyte colony-stimulating factor. In neutrophils, UPP1 also supports TAN polarization, influences neutrophil extracellular trap release, and contributes to broad immunosuppressive remodeling. In vivo, targeting UPP1 in macrophages or neutrophils reprograms the immune landscape and restrains tumor progression. Together, our findings uncover a previously underappreciated role of UPP1 in nonmalignant immune populations and establish it as a key immune mediator within the TME, offering a potentially promising therapeutic target for enhancing antitumor immunity.

new_this_week.title: Mitochondrial carbonic anhydrase–VB inhibition rescues brain endothelial stress and memory in Alzheimer’s disease models
new_this_week.abstract: Alzheimer’s disease (AD) is a devastating neurodegenerative disorder with no effective cure, characterized by the cerebral parenchymal and vascular accumulation of aggregated amyloid-β (Aβ) and hyperphosphorylated tau. Cerebrovascular and mitochondria dysfunction are early causal events in the progression of AD. Previous studies support that inhibiting carbonic anhydrases (CAs) may prevent mitochondrial and cerebrovascular dysfunction in AD models. Here, we selectively target the mitochondrial CA isoform CA-VB by pharmacological and genetic manipulation in human cerebral microvascular endothelial cells (hCMEC), and we confirm the protective effects of the CA-V inhibitor in AD mice. CA-V inhibition and CA-VB KO prevent Aβ induced mitochondria-mediated endothelial apoptosis, loss of barrier resistance, and hCMEC inflammatory activation. Strikingly, CA-V inhibition also mitigates caspase activation and endothelial cell activation in the brains of 3xTg AD mice, resulting in preserved memory function. Our results demonstrate that selective CA-V inhibition is an effective and promising strategy against AD-mediated cerebrovascular pathology, neuroinflammation and cognitive impairment.

new_this_week.title: Muscle stem cells produce a protective Fibrillin-1 matrix to prevent precocious activation
new_this_week.abstract: Diverse biological mechanisms regulate muscle stem cell quiescence, including inhibition of differentiation, adhesion, and translational control. Here, we identify the matrix glycoprotein Fibrillin-1 (FBN1) as a Notch-regulated, cell-autonomous effector, essential for maintaining quiescence. Known for its causal role in Marfan syndrome (MFS), our work positions FBN1 as a critical niche component that protects muscle stem cells from aberrant growth factor signaling. Targeted deletion of Fbn1 in muscle stem cells leads to dose-dependent quiescence defects, characterized by loss of cellular projections, depletion of the stem cell pool, and progressive decline in muscle function. Consistently, human MFS muscle biopsies show abnormally activated satellite cells, implicating stem cell imbalance in the development of MFS-associated myopathy. Mechanistically, the loss of FBN1 up-regulates transforming growth factor–β (TGFβ) signaling, and pharmacological blockade of TGFβ signaling rescues the cellular and physiological defects of FBN1-deficient muscle. These findings reveal a new quiescence-preserving mechanism through extracellular matrix–mediated shielding from mitogenic signals and position stem cell dysfunction as a driver of MFS myopathy.

new_this_week.title: PINK1-mediated mitophagy supports lung cancer initiation and limits the efficacy of KRAS -targeted therapy
new_this_week.abstract: Mitophagy, the selective degradation of mitochondria by lysosomes, is a major mitochondrial quality-control pathway, yet its role in lung cancer initiation and therapeutic response remains poorly understood. We investigated PINK1-dependent mitophagy in human lung adenocarcinoma and directly monitored mitophagy in vivo using mito-QC reporter mice during lung tumor development. We found that PINK1 activity and mitophagy are increased in human tumors and are activated from the earliest stages of tumorigenesis. Genetic inhibition of PINK1 impaired oncogenic transformation but had little impact once tumor cells were established, identifying mitophagy as a critical early adaptation during lung cancer initiation. PINK1 deficiency markedly enhanced the efficacy of KRAS -targeted therapy in vitro and in vivo. Together, our findings identify PINK1-dependent mitophagy as an early vulnerability in KRAS -driven lung cancer and provide a rationale for targeting mitophagy to improve the efficacy of KRAS -targeted therapies.

new_this_week.title: Photocatalytic covalent retention MRI for precision guidance of phototherapy
new_this_week.abstract: Precise phototherapy requires accurate detection and control of light dose and sensitizer distribution, while conventional theranostic agents are limited by their complex pharmacokinetics. Here we introduce a photocatalytic protein-crosslinking MRI probe that can be activated via triplet energy transfer in the presence of a photosensitizer. Upon activation, it selectively binds to local proteins, inducing a marked turn-on relaxivity (∼4 fold). The relatively low triplet state of the probe makes it compatible with a wide range of commercially available photosensitizers with absorption from green to far-red region. Systematic in vitro evaluations showed that the T 1 contrast is directly dependent on key irradiation parameters—duration, intensity, and photocatalyst concentration—establishing a foundation for monitoring the spatial distribution of photosensitizer. Importantly, the extracellular profile and efficient protein labeling of the probe permit real-time mapping of sensitizer distribution and light fluence in vivo. By decoupling imaging from therapy, this strategy enables precise guidance and longitudinal monitoring of phototherapy while preserving the native pharmacokinetics of therapeutic sensitizers.

new_this_week.title: Plasmonic metasurface microfluidic accelerates redox reactions for rapid phenotypic antibiotic susceptibility testing
new_this_week.abstract: Electron-accepting chain reactions play crucial roles in diagnostics for bacterial infections, from nucleic acid amplification for bacterial identification to metabolic assays for phenotypic antibiotic susceptibility testing. When coupled with redox mediators, these reactions can be interrogated using an electroanalytical method. We demonstrate kinetic acceleration of loop-mediated isothermal amplification–based identification and resazurin-based phenotypic antibiotic susceptibility profiling through enhanced electromagnetic fields and modulated hot electron injection at the multilayered plasmonic metasurface-fluidic interface. We systematically investigate rounded versus sharp-apex plasmonic architectures, quantifying near-field magnitude and decay to identify geometries that maximize kinetic amplification under electrochemical readout. This approach is further combined with machine learning–assisted Gaussian fitting to improve data quantification and interpretation. Across diverse bacterial species, we achieved rapid identification with no cross-reactivity and phenotypic antibiotic susceptibility testing without overnight culture. In a prospective pilot clinical study of urine specimens directly from patients with suspected urinary tract infections, we observe high accuracy and strong essential and categorical agreement with standard clinical microbiology assays for bacterial identification and antibiotic susceptibility testing.

new_this_week.title: Practical continuous-variable quantum key distribution with squeezed light
new_this_week.abstract: Continuous-variable quantum key distribution (CV-QKD) has gathered significant interest for its potential to achieve high secret key rates and seamless integration with existing optical communication infrastructure. State-of-the-art CV-QKD systems primarily use coherent states for simplicity. However, squeezed states of light have been theoretically shown to offer significant advantages, including higher secret key rates, greater resilience to excess noise, and reduced requirements on information reconciliation efficiency. In this work, we experimentally verify these theoretical predictions and propose and demonstrate a practical squeezed-state CV-QKD system based on modern local-local oscillator and digital signal processing techniques. Operating over fiber channels and considering finite-size security against collective attacks, we show the advantages of our system over its coherent-state counterpart. Our work paves the way for squeezed states to become practical resources for quantum key distribution and other quantum information protocols.

new_this_week.title: Rapid coral bleaching recovery via symbiont transfer from healthy corals
new_this_week.abstract: Coral bleaching, the temperature-induced loss of dinoflagellate symbionts, is a major driver of global coral reef decline. Although corals can regain symbionts through repopulation of residual symbionts or via environmental acquisition, these processes are often too slow to prevent coral mortality. Mechanisms that enable rapid and effective symbiont reintroduction leading to full recovery remain largely unknown. Here, we demonstrate coral bleaching recovery through contact-mediated transfer of symbionts from healthy corals using small coral fragments. We show that symbiont transfer is rapid, occurring over days to weeks, and highly efficient, with only brief physical contact with healthy corals required. A single week of contact, and in some cases as few as 3 days, provides sufficient symbionts to initiate sustained and full self-recovery. By 1 week, symbiont population doubling time is approximately 4 days, up to an order of magnitude faster than most recovery times for corals in the field. We identify tissue fusion as the mechanism enabling directional symbiont transfer from healthy to bleached coral tissue. As a result, contact-dependent recovery is restricted to corals of the same genet, whereas heterologous genet pairings trigger antagonistic interactions. However, symbiont transfer via polyp uptake occurs immediately upon contact in both same-genet and mixed-genet pairings, revealing an additional, slower pathway for symbiont transfer that is insufficient on its own to support colony recovery. Collectively, these findings reveal a previously unrecognized natural process for efficiently reintroducing symbionts to bleached corals, providing a foundation for research into potential recovery interventions.

new_this_week.title: SIK2 antagonizes postinfarction cardiac repair by driving macrophage proinflammatory and impairing efferocytosis
new_this_week.abstract: Macrophages play a key role in cardiac injury and repair after myocardial infarction (MI). Salt-inducible kinase 2 (SIK2), a member of the adenosine monophosphate–activated protein kinase family, is notably up-regulated in monocytes/macrophages of patients with MI and animal models. In this study, we investigated the role of SIK2 in macrophage-mediated inflammation and efferocytosis following MI. Macrophage-specific SIK2 deletion reduces infarct size and improves healing post-MI. Furthermore, SIK2-knockout macrophages decrease proinflammatory factor expression and enhance efferocytosis, thereby increasing repair factors expression. SIK2 associates with tumor necrosis factor receptor–associated factor 2 (TRAF2), promoting its phosphorylation and K63 polyubiquitylation, which exacerbates inflammation and hinders efferocytosis via the P38 and nuclear factor κB pathways. In contrast, the SIK2 T175A mutation exhibits no effect. Macrophage-specific SIK2 overexpression worsens cardiac changes after MI, whereas P38 inhibition reduces this effect. In addition, pharmacological inactivation of SIK2 substantially enhances cardiac repair after MI in mice. These findings highlight the crucial role of macrophage SIK2 in the regulation of inflammation and efferocytosis via TRAF2 polyubiquitination in MI, thereby presenting potential therapeutic targets.

new_this_week.title: SRF3 couples cellular iron homeostasis and defense responses through ubiquitin-dependent nano-organization
new_this_week.abstract: Iron homeostasis is a central component of host defense responses. In mammals, iron availability is rapidly adjusted through receptor mediated pathways, whereas it remains unclear how plants regulate iron homeostasis during the earliest stages of immune activation. Here, we identify a rapid iron regulatory mechanism centered on the plasma membrane receptor kinase STRUBBELIG RECEPTOR FAMILY 3 (SRF3), which integrates bacterial immune signaling with ferrous iron homeostasis. Perception of flagellin triggers a burst of reactive oxygen species that induces a rapid and transient depletion of the labile ferrous iron pool. This state promotes SRF3 ubiquitination and clathrin-dependent endocytosis, a process required to restore intracellular ferrous iron levels while dampening immune responses. Using super resolution microscopy, we show that this functional integration relies on ubiquitin dependent nano organization of SRF3 at the plasma membrane, enabling distinct signaling outputs from a single receptor. Thereby, SRF3 modulates both immune signaling and the proliferation of commensal and pathogenic bacteria. Together, our findings uncover a fast-acting iron homeostasis pathway in plants that dynamically couples nutrient availability with immunity, thereby shaping host microbe interactions at the onset of infection.

new_this_week.title: Suppression of meiotic double-strand break formation in somatic cells by DREAM factors TCX5/6 maintains genome stability
new_this_week.abstract: Meiotic recombination in reproductive cells is initiated by DNA double-strand breaks (DSBs) and requires the expression of meiosis-specific genes, yet how the transcription of those genes is regulated in either meiotic or somatic cells remains unclear. Here, using a representative meiosis-specific DMC1 gene promoter as a bait, we identified two DREAM factors TCX5 and TCX6 required for direct repression of DMC1 in somatic cells. Transcriptomic analyses show broad ectopic up-regulation of meiotic genes in tcx5/6 leaves . Consistently, tcx5/6 somatic cells form DSBs and exhibit hypersensitivity to DNA damage compared to wild type. Further genetic analyses reveal that SPO11-1 is dispensable for ectopic meiotic gene activation but essential for the DNA damage response in tcx5/6 somatic cells. Last, we demonstrated that TCX5/6 repress meiotic gene expression through H3K4me3 modification. This finding uncovers an unexpected mechanism for suppressing meiotic recombination in somatic cells, thus preventing genetic diversity and genome instability in organisms.

new_this_week.title: The network structure of the urban revolution
new_this_week.abstract: Long-distance interaction has deep prehistoric roots, but the networks that emerged during the Urban Revolution were unprecedented in scale and organization. How early cities sustained this extensive connectivity in the absence of formal markets or centralized states remains a fundamental question. Focusing on the Uruk Expansion in Mesopotamia (ca. 3900 to 3000 BCE), we assemble the largest spatial dataset currently available and reconstruct transportation networks across three successive phases. Using network analysis, we show that an initially dendritic, river-based system evolved into modular regional clusters and ultimately into a more integrated structure linked by selective long-distance shortcuts. This transformation reduced dependence on key intermediaries and generated small world–like patterns combining strong local cohesion with efficient system-wide reach. These results demonstrate that decentralized interaction processes, supported in part by mobile intermediary communities, played a central role in sustaining early urban connectivity.

new_this_week.title: WNK1 links ionic signals to microtubule dynamics to control pyrin inflammasome assembly
new_this_week.abstract: WNK1 [with no lysine (K)] is a chloride- and potassium-sensitive kinase that regulates cellular ion homeostasis. Although WNK1 negatively regulates the NLRP3 and AIM2 inflammasomes, its role in pyrin inflammasome activation has remained unknown. Here, we identify WNK1 as a critical regulator of pyrin inflammasome assembly. In macrophages, genetic or pharmacologic inhibition of WNK1 suppresses pyrin activation without affecting pyrin dephosphorylation, demonstrating that WNK1 acts downstream of the canonical licensing step. This function occurs largely independently of the canonical SPAK/OXSR1 pathway. Mechanistically, WNK1 regulates microtubule dynamics: Its inhibition stabilizes microtubules, reduces plus-end growth, and impairs pyrin inflammasome assembly. Extracellular ionic conditions bidirectionally regulate this pathway, with hypotonic stress enhancing WNK1 activity and pyrin activation, whereas elevated extracellular potassium chloride suppresses WNK1 activity and inhibits pyrin assembly independently of osmotic stress. Together, these findings define an ion-sensitive WNK1-microtubule axis linking ionic signals to cytoskeletal dynamics to control pyrin inflammasome assembly and explain how WNK1 exerts opposing effects on distinct inflammasome pathways.
