new_this_week.title: Aberrant one-carbon metabolism and ancestral genetics underlie edematous severe acute malnutrition
new_this_week.abstract: Abstract Edematous severe childhood malnutrition is distinct from the non-edematous form of malnutrition and remains a major cause of under-five mortality. Its etiology remains unclear, although aberrant one-carbon metabolism has emerged as a potential contributor. Here, we assess genetic variants at loci known to influence one-carbon metabolism, and determine their association with edematous malnutrition in Jamaica and Malawi. Six loci show evidence of association, including four related to homocysteine and folate metabolism - AHCYL1 , PRICKLE2 , GABBR2 , and PLD2 , with SNPs at the latter three also having direct effects on homocysteine-related metabolites in Mendelian Randomization. Collectively, one-carbon metabolism-related variants were significantly associated with edematous malnutrition (z = 3.2), with population differences linked to a shared East African genetic ancestry and distinct signatures of selection. These findings strengthen evidence implicating aberrant one-carbon metabolism in edematous malnutrition and highlight the utility of cell-free DNA, intra-continental admixture, and population genetics for mapping disease risk.

new_this_week.title: Closed-loop upcycling of residual lithium in LiFePO4 into tunable thin lithium metal electrodes
new_this_week.abstract: Abstract With the rapid development of electric vehicles, massive quantities of spent lithium iron phosphate batteries are generated, creating an urgent demand for efficient and sustainable recycling. Here we show a redox mediator-assisted strategy that directly converts simulated spent lithium iron phosphate powder into thin lithium metal, reducing energy requirements and enabling regeneration of the redox mediator. The process achieves a 98% final lithium extraction and produces lithium foils with a preformed interphase, tolerating volume changes and resisting air corrosion. The recycled Li (4.14 mAh cm −2 ) enables Li | |Li cells to cycle over 1,200 h at the test condition of 1 mA cm −2 / 1 mAh cm −2 and shows stable interfacial resistance with reduced electrolyte decomposition. When paired with NCM811, the cells retain 91.4% capacity over 400 cycles at 0.2 C/0.3 C. This closed-loop process couples lithium recovery with designed electrode fabrication, providing an alternative pathway for sustainable battery recycling and negative electrode design.

new_this_week.title: Divergent asymmetric synthesis of (–)-ganocins A–C and (+)-cochlearol B via a non-biomimetic strategy
new_this_week.abstract: Abstract Natural products are of substantial value in drug discovery screening campaigns. Their three-dimensional structures exhibit high complementarity with target proteins, via a multimodal combination of hydrogen bonds, hydrophobic contacts, electrostatic interactions, and van der Waals interactions. Skeletal diversity directly determines the three-dimensional shape diversity of compound libraries. Therefore, the rapid access to distinct molecular skeletons significantly increases the odds of drug discovery. Ganocins A–C and cochlearol B, Ganoderma meroterpenoids, feature distinct skeletons and diverse bioactivities. Despite tremendous efforts by synthetic chemists, a unified asymmetric synthetic strategy towards all four members has remained elusive. Here, we report the unified, asymmetric total synthesis of (–)-ganocins A–C and (+)-cochlearol B via a non-biomimetic strategy, featuring diastereoselective oxa-Michael addition, acid-controlled divergent cascade aldol/etherification cyclization or aldol/dehydration, and SmI 2 -mediated 4- exo -trig reductive cross-coupling. This meticulously designed synthetic strategy establishes a general solution to a problem previously deemed intractable by biomimetic approaches.

new_this_week.title: Microscale spatial fragmentation promotes bacterial survival under antibiotics
new_this_week.abstract: Most bacteria inhabit fragmented microscale environments rather than well-mixed systems in which antibiotic efficacy is typically defined. Here, we show that microscale spatial fragmentation alone can deterministically promote bacterial survival under antibiotic exposure. A coarse-grained theoretical model predicts that, at fixed bulk cell density and antibiotic concentration, fragmentation generates refuges through two coupled mechanisms: slower growth, which reduces susceptibility to growth-dependent antibiotics, and a finite antibiotic-per-cell constraint that lowers the effective intracellular antibiotic concentration. Using a microdroplet platform spanning five orders of magnitude in volume, we experimentally confirm these predictions for β-lactams; we further demonstrate that the same fragmentation-mediated protection extends to antibiotics with distinct modes of action. Spatial fragmentation thus creates robust, non-genetic antibiotic refuges governed by physical constraints rather than resistance or collective protection, with implications for bacterial persistence in natural and clinical environments and for antibiotic design.

new_this_week.title: Photoreversible defect complexation dynamically modulates guest adsorption in metal-organic frameworks
new_this_week.abstract: Abstract Reversible light-driven adsorption in framework materials offers a route to energy-efficient separations, yet current mechanisms deliver modest working capacities that constrain practical utility. Here we introduce photo-reversible defect complexation as a design principle for enhancing light-induced working capacities, coupling photoswitch isomerisation to active binding site modulation rather than pore geometry changes alone. We exploit coordinatively unsaturated Zr sites in defective UiO-67 as reversible binding sites, where a grafted spiropyran (SP) photoswitch undergoes UV-induced isomerisation to the zwitterionic merocyanine (MC) form, whose phenolate oxygen coordinates an additional open Zr site, suppressing guest binding availability. Visible light fully reverses this process. This mechanism delivers an 83% enhancement in photo-modulated CO 2 working capacity, reaching 1.1 mmol g −1 , nearly double that of the structural analog of P-UiO that does not enable photo-reversible MC-defect switching. Light-controlled metal cation and CO 2 uptake confirms that binding site availability, rather than pore geometry, drives this switching response. Density functional theory (DFT) simulations and multimodal X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) confirm reversible MC-Zr site complexation as the operative mechanism with performance retained across multiple photocycles. These findings establish photo-reversible defect engineering as a robust and broadly applicable principle for light-responsive frameworks with modulable guest adsorption.

new_this_week.title: Spatial transcriptomics unveils the in situ cellular and molecular hallmarks of the lung in fatal COVID-19
new_this_week.abstract: Severe Coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) can induce progressive diffuse alveolar damage (DAD) leading to fatal outcomes. Here, we leveraged data from Visium spatial transcriptomics for COVID-19 and control lung samples to unravel insights into cellular and molecular events driving lethal COVID-19. We report a progressive loss of endothelial cell types, pneumocytes type I and natural killer cells coupled with a continuous increase of myeloid and stromal cells, mostly peribronchial fibroblasts, across acute and proliferative DAD. Spatial organization analysis also identified specific compartmentalization including immune-specific clusters across DAD patterns. Importantly, spatially informed ligand-receptor interaction analysis revealed intercellular communication signatures defining COVID-19 induced DAD. Transcription factor activity enrichment analysis identified the TGF-β pathway as DAD driver, highlighting the antagonizing roles of SMAD3 and SMAD7 activity during fibrosis. Integration of these data yielded a signaling kinase pathway in peribronchial fibroblasts with amenable novel targets. Finally, spatio-temporal trajectory analysis characterized an alveolar epithelium regeneration program. Here, Garcia-Prieto et al use spatial transcriptomics to reveal progressive endothelial, pneumocyte type I and natural killer cell loss, expansion of myeloid and stromal cells, TGF-β-driven fibrosis signaling and alveolar regeneration programs in fatal COVID-19 lung injury.

new_this_week.title: Thromboxane A2 receptor signalling amplifies osteoclastogenesis in rheumatoid arthritis through ACSL1 associated mitochondrial oxidative metabolism
new_this_week.abstract: Activated platelets contribute to inflammation in rheumatoid arthritis, but how platelet-derived signals promote bone erosion remains poorly understood. Here we show that thromboxane A2, a major mediator released by activated platelets, promotes the formation of bone-resorbing osteoclasts through the thromboxane A2 receptor. Markers of thromboxane A2 biosynthesis are increased in patients with rheumatoid arthritis, while pharmacological inhibition or genetic loss of its receptor suppresses osteoclastogenesis in mouse cells and mice. Integrated molecular analyses reveal that thromboxane A2 receptor signalling supports osteoclastogenesis by increasing fatty acid oxidation and acetyl-coenzyme A supply needed for mitochondrial energy metabolism, involving peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor gamma coactivator 1 beta, peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor gamma and acyl-coenzyme A synthetase long-chain family member 1. In male mice, receptor inhibition or genetic deletion reduces osteoclast accumulation and bone destruction. These findings identify thromboxane A2 signalling as a driver of inflammatory bone erosion and a potential therapeutic target in rheumatoid arthritis. Here, the authors show that thromboxane A2 receptor signalling promotes bone-resorbing osteoclast formation in rheumatoid arthritis by rewiring metabolism, while receptor blockade protects against bone damage in mice.

new_this_week.title: Tissue composition shapes differential skeletal integration strategies during axolotl limb regeneration
new_this_week.abstract: Abstract Limb regeneration requires rebuilding the missing structures and integrating them with stump tissues. Osteoclast-mediated tissue resorption is essential for skeletal integration during regeneration. However, it is unknown if skeletal tissue composition impacts its resorption and, if so, how it is regulated. Here, we show that osteoclast-mediated skeletal resorption is activated in amputations damaging the diaphysis, but not the epiphysis, of skeletal elements. We found that amputations in the calcified diaphysis trigger the sustained expression of RANKL and the chemokine Loc483 , and that the latter is sufficient to induce osteoclast presence in non-resorbing amputations. Finally, our data suggests that the transcriptomic profile of the apical epithelial cap is impacted by the tissues injured by the amputation. Overall, our work reveals that tissue composition at the amputation plane shapes adaptations of the regenerative program, which ultimately contribute to the near-seamless tissue integration of the regenerating axolotl limb regardless of the amputation position.

new_this_week.title: Uhrf1 loss disrupts CTCF-associated chromatin organization during early mouse embryogenesis
new_this_week.abstract: UHRF1 is a chromatin-binding protein essential for maintaining DNA methylation and histone modification states, yet its integrated role in vivo remains incompletely understood. To define its function, we generated conditional Uhrf1 knockout embryonic stem cells (ESCs) and embryos. Uhrf1⁻/⁻ ESCs exhibited near-complete loss of 5mC and 5hmC but maintained pluripotency, whereas Uhrf1-null embryos developed normally until E8.5 and then failed to develop further by E9.5, phenocopying Dnmt1 loss. Single-cell multi-omic (ME-seq) profiling of E8.5 embryos revealed impaired lineage stabilization, widespread hypomethylation, and disrupted chromatin architecture. Uhrf1 loss was associated with altered CTCF-associated chromatin signal, broad remodeling of chromatin contacts, altered cis-regulatory relationships, and reduced predicted BMP-related ligand–receptor communication, particularly within neural crest populations. These findings identify Uhrf1 as a central regulator that tightly couples DNA methylation maintenance to 3D genome organization during gastrulation, thereby, directing early lineage specification and positioning Uhrf1 as a pivotal mediator of epigenetic information transfer during early embryogenesis. Highlights Uhrf1 knockout ESCs show global loss of 5mC/5hmC but maintain pluripotency. Uhrf1-null embryos develop normally until E8.5 but die by E9.5 with severe defects. Single-cell multi-omics revealed disrupted chromatin, transcription, and lineage stability upon knockout. Loss of Uhrf1 alters CTCF-associated chromatin signal, predicted BMP-related communication, and cis-regulatory relationships. Graphical abstract

new_this_week.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
new_this_week.title: Abiotic conversion of nitrate to ammonium enhances nitrogen use efficiency in paddy soils
new_this_week.abstract: Nitrogen (N) use efficiency is critical in ensuring food production while reducing nitrate (NO 3 − -N) to ammonium (NH 4 + -N) is widely recognized as a key for reducing N loss from paddy fields. Microbial involvement has long been regarded as the indispensable step for NO 3 − -N reduction to NH 4 + -N in nature; it remains largely unknown whether abiotic processes can drive this. Here, using laser confocal fluorescence microscopy and thermodynamic laws, we find that Fe(II) ions in the rice rhizosphere exist on iron plaque in a specific manner with strong reducing capability. These specifically adsorbed Fe(II) ions (Fe(II) SA ) could mediate the abiotic reduction of NO 3 − -N to NH 4 + -N, accounting for 57% of the total NO 3 − -N reduction. When cultured in a sterile nutrient solution containing only 15 NO 3 − -N and Fe(II) ions, over 90% of N in the xylem of rice plants exists as 15 NH 4 + -N, directly proving the occurrence of NO 3 − -N reduction to NH 4 + -N and taken up by rice. Theoretical calculations elucidate the Fe(II) SA -induced local electron depolarization enhances interfacial charge transfer which drives this reaction with the conversion of *NO to *NOH/*NHO identified as the rate-limiting step. We then propose a regulatory strategy to establish a stable Fe(II) SA /Fe(III) SA cycle utilizing FeC for controlled-release of Fe(II) ions. Two-year field experiments confirmed this strategy can increase rice yield by 16.1% while cutting half of the N input. Our work enables the design of novel pathways in improving N use efficiency for sustainable rice production.

new_this_week.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
new_this_week.title: Environmental chemical mixtures reprogram mammary epithelial development to epigenetic states associated with breast cancer
new_this_week.abstract: Environmental exposures occur as complex mixtures, yet the mechanisms by which they alter human tissue development and generate cancer-relevant tissue states remain poorly defined. Here, we establish a physiologically relevant 3D human breast organoid high-content screening platform that relates exposure-induced developmental disruption to cancer-relevant cell states. Screening of structurally diverse environmental chemicals as single agents and mixtures reveals heterogeneous but reproducible developmental responses, indicating that distinct environmental chemicals perturb different aspects of mammary morphogenesis. Focusing on bisphenols, we show that a low-dose mixture (BPA, BPS, and BPF; 3BPX) disrupts organoid development and induces transcriptional programs characterized by extracellular matrix remodeling, epithelial plasticity, and partial epithelial–mesenchymal transition, accompanied by widespread DNA methylation remodeling. A 3BPX exposure signature maps to ER+ luminal breast cancers and is preferentially enriched in invasive lobular carcinoma (ILC), a subtype characterized by epithelial plasticity. The 3BPX-associated methylation signature is detectable in primary tumors and adjacent normal tissue and is enriched in ILC. Together, these findings show that environmentally relevant chemical mixtures induce heterogeneous developmental perturbations that converge on conserved transcriptional and epigenetic programs associated with epithelial plasticity and tissue remodeling. These exposure-associated signatures are represented in defined epithelial and stromal compartments in human breast cancers, supporting a model in which developmental exposures may establish field-like, cancer-relevant tissue states.

new_this_week.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
new_this_week.title: Estimating the threat of AI-agent responding across online survey platforms
new_this_week.abstract: Recent research and advances in LLMs have led to widespread concern that AI agents could pose as human online survey-takers. However, it remains unclear how prevalent AI agents are on survey research platforms and how to effectively detect AI agents. We validated a series of AI detection tests that effectively separated verified-human participants from both prompted commercial and purpose-built AI agents. Using these tests, we collected surveys on seven online platforms and find wide variation in rates of respondents failing AI tests, ranging from 6 to 41% across platforms (compared to a 2.4% false-positive rate for in-person human participants). We further demonstrate that undetected AI agents can impact the results of online surveys. Our findings suggest that while there is an urgent need for AI detection tests and consistent, systematic monitoring of data quality on online platforms, some platforms currently appear to provide data with a low rate of AI agents.

new_this_week.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
new_this_week.title: FOXG1 spatiotemporally orchestrates subtype fate specification and patch/matrix identity of striatal spiny projection neurons
new_this_week.abstract: The striatum consists of three main spiny projection neuron subtypes, direct-pathway neurons (dSPNs), indirect-pathway neurons (iSPNs), and recently identified eccentric striatal neurons (eSPNs) with these SPNs organized into two complementary compartments, the patch and the matrix. However, the cellular basis underlying subtype specification especially that of eSPNs, and mechanisms governing the complementary patterning remain unclear. Here, employing single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) combined with loss-of-function we reveal that eSPNs share more developmental similarities with iSPNs and the transcription factor Foxg1 promotes dSPN and iSPN fates but suppresses eSPN fate in ventral region of the lateral ganglionic eminence lineage. Deletion of Foxg1 in progenitors forces both dSPNs and iSPNs into an eSPN fate. While postmitotic Foxg1 deletion impairs patch/matrix identity and leads to SPN aggregation. We identify FOXG1-driven transcriptional programs and key transcription factors that specify each striatal SPN subtype and patch/matrix identity, and uncover FOXG1 directly regulated cell migration- and cell adhesion-related molecules that control SPN migration. Our findings provide insights into striatal development.

new_this_week.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
new_this_week.title: LEAP2 mediates long-term inhibition of orexigenic neurons of the hypothalamus in mice
new_this_week.abstract: Liver-expressed antimicrobial peptide 2 (LEAP2) acts via the growth hormone secretagogue receptor (GHSR) to reduce food intake, yet the central mechanisms underlying its anorectic effects remain unclear. Here, we show that circulating LEAP2 accesses discrete brain regions, including the arcuate nucleus of the hypothalamus (ARH), where it targets orexigenic AgRP/NPY neurons. Despite the negligible local expression in the hypothalamus, LEAP2 peptide is detectable in this brain region and in the cerebrospinal fluid, suggesting peripheral origin and central retention. Using fluorescent tracers, in vivo, ex vivo, and in vitro approaches indicate that LEAP2 exhibits prolonged binding to GHSR at the plasma membrane without promoting receptor internalization, thereby limiting subsequent ghrelin action. Using male mice, we found that central or systemic LEAP2 pretreatment results in a sustained inhibition of ghrelin-induced feeding that lasts for several hours after pretreatment. Notably, LEAP2 also suppresses food intake and c-Fos induction triggered by pharmacogenetic activation of AgRP neurons, indicating a broader inhibitory control over these circuits. Together, our findings establish that LEAP2 acts as a persistent inhibitor of hypothalamic orexigenic centers, providing a mechanistic framework for its long-lasting anorectic effects. These results highlight LEAP2 as a key regulator of energy balance and support its potential as a therapeutic target for obesity and metabolic disorders.

new_this_week.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
new_this_week.title: Microbial niche partitioning explains N <sub>2</sub> O distributions and cycling in marine oxygen minimum zones
new_this_week.abstract: Oxygen minimum zones (OMZs) are marine hotspots for cycling and emission of the powerful greenhouse gas nitrous oxide (N 2 O). Steep redox gradients host diverse microbial communities that produce and consume N 2 O, generating a characteristic vertical distribution, with low concentrations in anoxic cores and supersaturated accumulation in surrounding oxyclines. Although the accumulation is commonly attributed to stronger O 2 inhibition of N 2 O consumption than production, this differential inhibition is not consistently observed, suggesting that interactions among nitrogen-cycling metabolisms may provide additional mechanisms. To evaluate the ecological controls on the N 2 O profile, we embed a trait-based ecosystem model into an eddy-resolving simulation of the Eastern Tropical South Pacific OMZ. In this framework, redox energetics, metabolite exchange, competition, and grazing structure microbial growth, setting emergent niches of microbial functional types, particularly aerobic ammonia oxidizers and diverse anaerobic denitrifiers that mediate N 2 O cycling. In the anoxic core, cross-feeding tightly couples denitrifiers that produce and consume N 2 O, maintaining low concentrations. As O 2 increases in the oxycline, competition with aerobic metabolisms and intensified grazing gradually exclude denitrifiers. However, because they draw on more abundant substrates, N 2 O-producing denitrifiers persist to higher O 2 than N 2 O consumers, reflecting the vulnerability of populations dependent on intermediate metabolites. This ecological decoupling drives N 2 O accumulation and captures the characteristic double-peaked vertical structure without imposing physiological O 2 intolerance thresholds. More broadly, by revealing how niche partitioning and producer–consumer coupling shape other features of OMZ biogeochemistry, these results provide a basis for projecting future shifts in marine nitrogen loss and N 2 O emissions.

new_this_week.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
new_this_week.title: Quantum-enhanced sensing of molecular excited-state dynamics with correlated photons
new_this_week.abstract: Squeezed photons, which provide a quantum-correlated light with reduced noise, have emerged as a powerful resource for sensing the structures of matter. Here, we study the pump–probe scheme using squeezed photons whose spectral correlation of amplitudes can be tailored. A microscopic theory reveals a highly time-energy-resolved signal that is not attainable by classical pump–probe scheme. The results show high selectivity of accessing the molecular correlation functions, e.g., suppression of ground-state bleaching signal, and can significantly enhance signal intensity that surpasses the bottleneck by entangled twin photons. An application to a monolayer semiconductor model reveals a real-time monitoring of valley excitons and their dynamics, i.e., conversion between dark and bright excitons. We further show the intermediate squeezing regime–not strong squeezing–where time-resolved spectroscopy is favorable. Our work offers a paradigm for studying nonequilibrium dynamics of matter, in photocatalysis and optoelectronics.

new_this_week.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
new_this_week.title: Restructuring hydrogen-bonding networks via hydroxyl-functionalized covalent organic frameworks for efficient nitrate electroreduction
new_this_week.abstract: Electrocatalytic nitrate reduction reaction (NO 3 RR) is a promising strategy for nitrate removal and ammonia synthesis, but its efficiency is largely limited by sluggish proton transfer kinetics and poor reaction selectivity. Herein, we rationally design a series of hydroxyl-functionalized copper phthalocyanine-based covalent organic frameworks (Cu-COF-nOH) to regulate interfacial proton transfer via restructuring hydrogen-bonding networks. The hydroxyl functional groups in Cu-COF-nOH enhance water adsorption and dissociation to enrich interfacial proton supply. Optimized hydroxyl loading further induces the formation of continuous hydrogen-bond chains, enabling oriented and accelerated proton shuttling toward Cu active centers instead of stochastic diffusion. Electrocatalytic tests in 0.5 M nitrate electrolyte show that the optimal Cu-COF-4OH catalyst achieves an ammonia Faradaic efficiency of 93.20% and an NH 3 yield rate of 65.84 mg·h −1 , along with excellent long-term stability, outperforming most state-of-the-art NO 3 RR electrocatalysts. Combined with in situ characterizations and theoretical calculations, we clearly clarify that hydroxyl-mediated hydrogen-bonding restructuring plays a critical role in boosting proton transfer kinetics and reaction selectivity. This work provides a versatile interface engineering strategy for efficient multiproton/electron-coupled electrocatalytic reactions, offering insights into the design of high-performance NO 3 RR catalysts.

new_this_week.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
new_this_week.title: Structure-based targeting of Atg8 uncovers its essential role in autophagy-mediated detoxification
new_this_week.abstract: Autophagy degrades and recycles intracellular material, allowing cells to maintain homeostasis and adapt to environmental stress. In the rice blast fungus Magnaporthe oryzae , the core autophagy protein MoAtg8 is required for autophagosome formation and host infection. Here, we determined the crystal structure of MoAtg8 and used it for structure-guided virtual screening of a focused compound library enriched for natural products and autophagy-related molecules. This screen identified nordihydroguaiaretic acid (NDGA), a naturally occurring lignan, as a MoAtg8-binding compound. NDGA suppressed conidial germination and appressorium formation, disrupted membrane integrity, and reduced pathogenicity in M. oryzae , with no detectable phytotoxicity to rice under the conditions tested. Mechanistically, the 5-lipoxygenase Mo5Lox, a target of NDGA, bound NDGA with lower affinity than MoAtg8. MoAtg8 associated with NDGA through Gln81 and promoted its autophagy-dependent delivery to vacuoles, thereby reducing compound availability to toxicity-associated targets. Disruption of autophagy or mutation of Gln81 in MoAtg8 increased fungal sensitivity to NDGA. These findings identify an autophagy-mediated detoxification route for an exogenous antifungal compound and reveal how MoAtg8-dependent trafficking modulates NDGA efficacy in a plant-pathogenic fungus.

new_this_week.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
new_this_week.title: Suspected distortion of citations in high-impact cancer journals
new_this_week.abstract: Research and scholarship are shaped by article citations, which underpin the communication of ideas, assignment of credit, journal impact factors, and author career progression. Given their key influence on author and journal metrics, citations can be intentionally manipulated to inflate the reputation of journals and researchers. Paper mills, unethical organizations that produce and sell manuscripts and publishing services, may also be manipulating citations, but the extent of this manipulation is unknown. Here, we show that molecular cancer articles sharing features with retracted papers from paper mills display citation patterns that suggest systematic inflation. These articles were published in journals in the top decile of journal rankings. Suspected paper mill articles received 50 to 100% more citations than other papers 1 to 3 y after publication, while paradoxically attracting fewer readers and online accesses. Suspected paper mill articles also cited—and were cited by—other suspected paper mill articles, which frequently appeared in journals previously reported as paper mill targets. Citations from suspected paper mill articles measurably inflated journal citation metrics. These findings suggest that paper mills inflate the citation metrics of supported publications and affected journals at scale. This widespread manipulation of citation metrics may amplify unreliable findings, slowing scientific progress and spurring unreasonable citation benchmarks for research articles, journals, and authors. Our findings point to measurable signatures of citation manipulation that could support article- and journal-level screening.

new_this_week.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
new_this_week.title: Synthetic reconstitution of planar polarity initiation reveals principles of symmetry breaking across scales
new_this_week.abstract: Development often relies on molecular prepatterning over large tissue scales, and how these patterns emerge is an essential question. Planar cell polarity (PCP), manifested as asymmetric distribution of junctional proteins within individual cells and coordinated across entire tissues, is a key module controlling tissue morphogenesis and organization. How tissues break symmetry to initiate PCP remains unknown. By reconstituting polarity initiation ex vivo using engineered epithelial cells, we found that collective migration acts as the symmetry-breaking cue, inducing front–back enrichment of CELSR junctions and establishing aligned multicellular CELSR polarity. Individual cells directly interpret the migration cue and remain sensitive to it. Strikingly, CELSR polarity arises without reciprocal VANGL–FZD interactions, identifying CELSR as the driver for polarity initiation. These findings reveal that collective migration initiates and coordinates PCP across molecular, cellular, and tissue scales, demonstrating that morphogenetic events act as a trigger for spatial pattern emergence.

new_this_week.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
new_this_week.title: The historical domestication of a Clostridium botulinum strain used for the industrial production of botulinum neurotoxin
new_this_week.abstract: Laboratory production of botulinum neurotoxin (BoNT) began more than 90 y ago for medical, military, and later pharmaceutical applications, creating one of the longest-running examples of microbial cultivation under sustained human control. A single Clostridium botulinum Group I lineage, Army Hall A (AHA), was established by the US military in 1942 and later gave rise to Hall A-hyper (HAH), the strain widely used for pharmaceutical BoNT production. We analyzed more than 1,000 C. botulinum genomes to identify AHA’s closest relatives and to infer the most recent common ancestor (MRCA) shared with its nearest lineage. Relative to this MRCA, AHA accumulated nearly 100 genetic changes, including 46 single-nucleotide substitutions, 44 small insertions or deletions, and several large deletions and structural variants that led to the loss of more than 80 genes. A nonsense mutation in mutS generated a hypermutator phenotype that accelerated mutation rates and increased genetic diversity. This event is inferred to have occurred early in the lineage’s domestication and appears to have facilitated laboratory-adaptive traits, including the lack of sporulation and increased BoNT yield. Competition experiments under standard growth conditions confirmed substantial laboratory adaptation, with AHA exhibiting a strong fitness advantage over a close relative. Together, these results reconstruct the genomic trajectory of a bacterium evolving under prolonged human-mediated selection and provide a genome-resolved example of microbial domestication. The findings show how laboratory conditions, industrial selection, and changing mutation rates can shape bacterial evolution, and they offer a general framework for understanding domestication and laboratory adaptation across microbial systems.

new_this_week.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
new_this_week.title: The impact of modulator therapy on the Pseudomonas aeruginosa cystic fibrosis lung transcriptome
new_this_week.abstract: Chronic lung infection with Pseudomonas aeruginosa is a major complication of cystic fibrosis (CF), contributing to lung function decline and increased morbidity and mortality. Laboratory models are used to study CF infections, but their relevance depends on how accurately they reproduce microbial physiology during human infection. We previously developed a framework that uses bacterial gene expression in human infections to quantify model accuracy. Here, we applied this framework to determine how a major therapeutic intervention impacts P. aeruginosa physiology in the lungs of people with CF (pwCF) and to develop and evaluate refined preclinical models. We focused on elexacaftor/tezacaftor/ivacaftor (ETI), a highly effective CFTR modulator therapy that has improved outcomes for pwCF. However, evidence indicates that P. aeruginosa lung infections persist despite ETI therapy. Analysis of P. aeruginosa transcriptomes from human sputum collected before and after ETI initiation revealed minimal changes in gene expression, indicating that the CF airway continues to support a similar bacterial transcriptional state despite therapy. We then evaluated how strain selection, zinc limitation, and polymicrobial coculture influence the ability of laboratory models to recapitulate P. aeruginosa gene expression in human CF sputum. Growth of CF clinical isolates in zinc-limited synthetic CF sputum medium produced the most accurate model, whereas population-based cultures and coculture with Staphylococcus aureus had limited effects. These findings show that ETI therapy has little impact on the conserved P. aeruginosa transcriptional state in human CF sputum and that refined sputum-like models remain useful for studying persistent infection in the postmodulator era.

new_this_week.title: A pair of chitosan receptors confer broad-spectrum fungal resistance
new_this_week.abstract: Chitosan, a major fungal cell wall component, activates plant immunity, yet the underlying perception mechanism remains unknown. In this study, we identified OsFID1, an apoplast-localized DUF26 domain protein, as a chitosan-binding receptor essential for chitosan-triggered immunity. OsFID1 forms a receptor complex with OsFID2, a plasma membrane–localized DUF26 receptor-like kinase, to mediate chitosan sensing and immune activation, requiring OsFID2 phosphorylation for function. The OsFID1-OsFID2 complex confers broad-spectrum resistance to fungal pathogens. OsFID1 homologs are conserved in land plants, which show chitosan-binding activity in both monocots and dicots. Ectopic expression of OsFID1 in wheat and maize enhanced fungal resistance without growth penalty. These findings uncover a conserved receptor complex for direct chitosan sensing, advancing our understanding of plant-fungus interactions and providing a potential strategy for engineering durable fungal resistance crops.

new_this_week.title: Atomic functional site scaffolding in biopolymers with RFdiffusion3
new_this_week.abstract: The catalytic and other sophisticated functions of biomolecules arise from the placement of many atoms in three-dimensional space. Here, we describe a generative artificial intelligence method for biopolymers, RFdiffusion3 (RFD3), which employs free atom diffusion to satisfy complex sets of atomic constraints more rapidly and accurately than previous methods across several challenges from enzyme design to RNA structure design. We demonstrate experimentally the power of the RFD3 pipeline for enzyme design by designing de novo phosphotriesterases with a complex active site architecture incorporating a carbamylated lysine coordinating two metal ions and zinc proteases specific for the transthyretin protein involved in amyloid diseases; in both cases we obtain active catalysts in zero shot 96 construct design campaigns.

new_this_week.title: Dendritic computation for abstract rule-based flexible decision-making
new_this_week.abstract: Intelligent behavior involves flexible integration of sensory input and abstract rule knowledge. Dendritic computation has been shown to contribute to top-down modulation of sensory processing; however, whether and how it is involved in flexible cognitive processing remains to be elucidated. Combining a rule-based flexible decision-making task with in vivo two-photon imaging and optogenetics in mice, we found that within single layer 5 extratelencephalic neurons in the auditory cortex, apical dendrites preferentially encoded the inferred abstract rule and somata preferentially represented sensory stimuli, whereas choice signals were present in both compartments. Optogenetic dendritic inhibition impaired rule-dependent somatic choice coding, supporting a task-relevant integration across the dendritic and somatic compartments. These results indicate that dendritic computation in cortical neurons mediates flexible behavior.

new_this_week.title: Glycan recognition by a plant damage-sensing immune receptor
new_this_week.abstract: Pathogens target and degrade the extracellular matrix surrounding plant cells. A central question is how cell wall-derived damage-associated molecular patterns (DAMPs) are recognized and integrated to trigger immune responses. We address this question by determining the structure of the extracellular multidomain of the IGP1 receptor in both apo form and bound to the cellulose-derived DAMP cellotriose. Structural analyses reveal that constitutive interactions of Leucine Rich Repeat (LRR)-malectin domains preconfigure IGP1 for ligand recognition and that the receptor features a highly specific sugar-binding pocket in the LRR domain capable of distinguishing fine variations in glycan structures. By directly sensing cello-oligomers, IGP1 operates as a cell wall surveillance receptor that links pathogen-induced wall degradation to immune alerting, equipping plants to mount rapid and robust defense responses.

new_this_week.title: Regulation of target gene expression by chromatin-associated protein-coding transcripts in plants
new_this_week.abstract: Protein-coding transcripts are regarded as intermediates that mediate DNA-to-protein information flow, leaving their noncoding regulatory potential largely underappreciated. Genome-wide profiling of RNA–chromatin interactions in Arabidopsis has uncovered widespread associations between protein-coding transcripts and distinct genomic loci, implying that they possess regulatory functions. Here, we found that BT2 and GSL8 transcripts modulate target gene transcription independently of their protein products through distinct mechanisms. The BT2 transcript represses transcription of its targets CEP2 and MRF4 by forming RNA–DNA triplexes, thereby restricting root growth and promoting flowering, whereas GSL8 acts through a triplex-independent pathway. Our findings unveil intrinsic regulatory activities of protein-coding transcripts, challenging the canonical definition of mRNA function and blurring the functional distinction between coding and noncoding RNAs in the context of genome evolution.

new_this_week.title: Structural basis for size-selective perception of chitin in plants
new_this_week.abstract: Plants detect microbes through pattern recognition receptors that perceive conserved microbial surface motifs known as microbe-associated molecular patterns (MAMPs). Lysin motif (LysM) receptors recognize and mediate downstream responses to chitinous MAMPs. In this study, we elucidated the mechanism for the specific recognition of long-chain chitin oligomers and identified a hallmark bridge domain characteristic of the CHITIN PERCEPTION (CHIP) receptor class. Structural analysis of receptor-ligand complexes, biochemistry, and in planta functional studies of inhibitory nanobodies revealed the mechanism of size-selective, high-affinity chitin perception in Lotus japonicus and Medicago truncatula . Additionally, we identified the CHITIN ELICITOR RECEPTOR KINASE (CERK) class as low-affinity, yet essential, co-receptors and propose a mechanistic model for a ligand-induced core signaling heterocomplex. Our findings establish the structural and mechanistic basis of differential chitin perception and receptor complex assembly in chitin-elicited plant immune signaling.
affiliations: Department of Chemistry, University of Copenhagen, Copenhagen, Denmark.
Department of Molecular Biology and Genetics, Aarhus University, Aarhus, Denmark.

new_this_week.title: To reverse nature loss, change what drives it
new_this_week.abstract: This week, at the 17th Meeting of the Conference of the Parties to the Convention on Biological Diversity (COP17), delegates from 195 countries and the European Union are gathering in Yerevan, Armenia, for a global review of progress under the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework, an international set of goals and targets adopted in 2022 to tackle the biodiversity crisis. The urgent question before them is clear: What must change now to halt and reverse nature’s decline and put it on a path to recovery by 2030? COP-17 comes as international cooperation is under increasing strain. Extreme weather is intensifying, ecosystem deterioration is creating new security risks, and geopolitical tensions are rising. Yet nature’s decline does not pause for geopolitical instability—it deepens it. That makes effective multilateralism, with North and South as equal partners, more important, not less.
affiliations: David Cooper is a fellow at the Leverhulme Centre for Nature Recovery, University of Oxford, UK, and former acting executive secretary of the Convention on Biological Diversity.

Sandra Díaz is a senior principal investigator at CONICET and professor at Universidad Nacional de Córdoba, Argentina, and former co-chair of the IPBES Global Assessment of Biodiversity and Ecosystem Services.

new_this_week.title: Spatiality of preemptive coercion: How autocrats demolish informal settlements for political control
new_this_week.abstract: Abstract Why do authorities demolish informal settlements in metropolises? The social sciences have a long tradition of addressing this issue through the lens of economic development or welfare provision. I instead propose a theory of political control. Autocrats adopt demolition as a preemptive and coercive tool to remove communities substantively and symbolically less legible to them, thereby ensuring societal compliance and restoring visual order. Empirically, I compile a unique dataset of 320 demolished and undemolished informal settlements in Beijing between 2017 and 2018, based on satellite imagery, digital street views, and fieldwork. The results indicate that the low legibility of informal settlements to authorities correlates with a greater likelihood of demolition. This paper contributes to the social science literature by connecting legibility politics with urban governance. It also introduces a spatial perspective and leverages novel data sources to deepen our understanding of preemptive coercion under authoritarianism.
affiliations: Department of Politics and International Studies SOAS University of London London United Kingdom

new_this_week.title: The link between three smartphone school policies and students’ mental health: a growth trajectory approach
new_this_week.abstract: Abstract Amid growing concerns about smartphones and students’ mental health, schools worldwide are introducing smartphone policies, often without evidence on their effectiveness. This longitudinal study examines how three naturally implemented policies (full restrictions, partial restrictions allowing use during lunchbreak, partial restrictions allowing use during lunch, and afternoon break) relate to mental health across one school year (up to seven waves). Differences were observed at the first measurement wave (two months after implementation): Students in the full-restriction school reported highest depressive symptoms and anxiety. Differences in life satisfaction were also observed without a clear pattern across policy types. Growth trajectory analyses revealed no significant differences in mental health changes over time. Yet, within schools, both the full-restrictions and the lunchbreak school showed increases in depressive symptoms. Life satisfaction decreased slightly in the lunchbreak school. These findings suggest that smartphone restrictions are not a simple solution to youth mental health challenges.
