new_this_week.title: A microexon regulatory code reveals autism-linked genetic variation
new_this_week.abstract: Abstract Neuronal microexons are a highly conserved class of alternative splicing events enriched in genes with critical functions in nervous system biology 1,2 . Microexon splicing is often disrupted in the brains of autistic individuals, and mice with microexon deficiencies display autism-like phenotypes 1,3,4 . However, the full landscape of microexons is not known, and the impact of genetic variation on these exons has not been systematically investigated. Here, through extensive transcriptome profiling, we detect hundreds of new microexons, including many with neuronal subtype-specific splicing patterns, and others that activate nonsense-mediated mRNA decay. Using machine learning, we define a sequence code predictive of neuronally spliced microexons and use this to identify critical regulatory elements surrounding the expanded microexon repertoire. This code further reveals genomic variants predicted to alter microexon splicing in individuals affected by autism, with rare variants having the strongest estimated impact. These variants are mostly detected in idiopathic individuals and are associated with autism status. They also converge on synaptic and other autism-linked genes, as well as genes not previously linked to autism. Our results collectively define an expanded repertoire of microexons, delineate their regulatory code, and pinpoint variants predicted to affect their splicing, with implications for the disruption of functions central to neuronal biology and brain disorders.
new_this_week.semantic_scholar_tldr: An expanded repertoire of microexons is defined, their regulatory code is delineated, and genomic variants predicted to alter microexon splicing in individuals affected by autism are revealed, with implications for the disruption of functions central to neuronal biology and brain disorders.

new_this_week.title: Competing mechanisms toughen bcc binary and medium-entropy alloys at 20 K
new_this_week.abstract: Abstract Plastic deformation in body-centred cubic (bcc) metals and alloys is conventionally mediated by screw dislocations. Their temperature-sensitive motion is attributed to a steep rise in strength with decreasing temperature that constricts plastic zones at crack tips, leading to a ductile-to-brittle transition 1 . Here we evaluated the mechanical properties of group IV–V bcc refractory alloys with similar electronic structures at 20 K and found that these materials instead exhibit a plateau in tensile yield strength and fracture toughness as a function of temperature, with no apparent ductile-to-brittle transition. This behaviour arises from the global activation of twinning and an ω-phase transformation, which nucleate dislocations at interfaces before global dislocation motion. The initial mechanism is temperature insensitive and controls yielding, thereby preventing a crack-tip plastic zone from constricting with decreasing temperature.

new_this_week.title: Computational design of metalloproteases
new_this_week.abstract: De novo design of enzymes that cleave amide bonds represents a major challenge1–2. Here we use RFdiffusion methods3–4 to de novo design proteins with water activating zinc based active sites adjacent to a peptide substrate binding pocket. Of 135 designs tested, 36% catalyze cleavage of their cognate peptide substrates at the targeted scissile bond. The best design accelerates peptide-bond hydrolysis by more than 108-fold relative to the uncatalyzed reaction; four substitutions increase this acceleration to over 1010-fold by improving active-site preorganization5. We use this approach to design metalloproteases that selectively cleave the human disease associated proteins TDP-43, amyloid-β, and serum amyloid A, with rate enhancements of up to 109-fold. We further design caged cytokines and receptor antagonists that are selectively activated by the designed proteases, enabling bioorthogonal control of cell state. Thus, de novo design can yield highly active, programmable proteases with applications in therapeutics, biotechnology, and bioremediation.

new_this_week.title: Educational intervention can rewire village social networks
new_this_week.abstract: Social networks shape behaviour, affect information dissemination and undergird collective action. And they can be exploited in the design of interventions in these domains1-7. Although social networks obey fundamental principles, such as the degree distribution8,9, they can nevertheless evolve as ties form and break. Here, through a randomized controlled trial involving a total of 8,331 people in 110 remote Honduran villages, we evaluate the secondary effects of a 22-month public-health intervention1 on pre-existing social-network structure. We used a design in which a varying fraction of village households received the intervention, and villages in which no one received the intervention were used as the primary reference group. In 'low-dosage' villages (in which 5-30% of households received the intervention), people who received the intervention tended to sever ties with untreated individuals to whom they previously went for health advice. Conversely, in high-dosage villages (50-100%), treated individuals increased their ties. These average changes are explained mainly by tie dynamics; that is, treated-treated pairs persist and form new links, whereas treated-untreated ties dissolve. A mediation analysis indicates that absorption of health information increases the likelihood of tie formation and persistence. The rewiring patterns generally lasted for three years after the intervention ceased. Moreover, although the intervention delivered health information, it reshaped friendship and financial ties, not just health-advice connections. In aggregate, the introduction of a new information regime acted as a kind of social institution, rewiring individuals' connections even though the overall degree distribution of village-wide networks remained relatively stable.

new_this_week.title: Parity-dependent coupling of molecular spin chains to a superconductor
new_this_week.abstract: Collective behaviour in quantum materials can produce excitations carrying only a fraction of the quantum numbers of their constituents. A notable case occurs in chains of spin-1 units1, in which a topological gap protects the interior of the chain, whereas spin-1/2 states, half the spin of the units that form it, emerge at the ends2. In short chains, these fractional edge spins couple to each other and their topological protection makes them attractive for hybrid spin–superconductor devices. Whether such fractionalization survives the proximity of a superconducting condensate, however, remains an open question. Here we grow molecular Haldane chains of antiferromagnetically coupled spin-1 triangulene units on a proximitized Au(111)/Nb(110) surface and resolve a parity-dependent coupling of their spin-1/2 edge states to the superconductor by scanning tunnelling spectroscopy. Odd-length chains host Yu–Shiba–Rusinov (YSR) bound states inside the superconducting gap, originating from a global S = 1 ground state, whereas even-length chains form an S = 0 ground state decoupled from the superconductor. A two-site model attributes this alternation to the sign and strength of inter-edge interactions, independently confirmed by extra-gap spin excitations in tunnelling spectra. Many-body spin excitations of the S = 1 chain are also detected, decoupled from the superconductor by the much larger Haldane gap. The length-tunable coupling of the edge spins to superconductors opens a route towards molecular spin qubits based on π-conjugated carbon architectures. Scanning tunnelling spectroscopy shows that the fractional spin-1/2 end states of molecular Haldane chains couple differently to a superconducting condensate depending on whether the chain contains an even or odd number of spin-1 triangulene units.

new_this_week.title: Sexual dimorphism in epidermal stem cell dynamics
new_this_week.abstract: Abstract The epidermis is a stratified epithelium comprising proliferative basal cells and differentiated suprabasal cells that are continuously renewed throughout life. Conflicting theories have been proposed regarding the heterogeneity of the basal cell layer, with some studies proposing that all proliferative cells have self-renewal potential during homeostasis 1–5 . Meanwhile, others posit a model in which stem cell differentiation occurs through an intermediate transit-amplifying-like progenitor state with strictly limited proliferative potential 6–10 . Here, to determine the heterogeneity and pattern of cell fate, we performed intravital time-lapse imaging to track the fate of lineage-labelled cells in the skin interfollicular epidermis. Results from quantitative analyses of clonal dynamics support a two-compartment model of epidermal homeostasis, whereby basal cells are organized in a stem cell–transit-amplifying cell hierarchy. Critical to these conclusions was the discovery of sexual dimorphism in epidermal fate, with female mice showing a highly synchronized pattern of cell division, differentiation and delamination that contributes to accelerated wound healing. Single-cell RNA sequencing, transcriptional profiling and clonal analyses of castrated mice revealed that male sex hormones promote stem cell differentiation and delamination. In summary, our study provides insight into the functional identity of the stem cell population and identifies sex-specific differences in the regulation of epidermal stem cells and transit-amplifying cell fate.
new_this_week.semantic_scholar_tldr: Insight is provided into the functional identity of the stem cell population and sex-specific differences in the regulation of epidermal stem cells and transit-amplifying cell fate and a two-compartment model of epidermal homeostasis is supported.

new_this_week.title: Wave coarsening drives time crystallization in mechatronic metamaterials
new_this_week.abstract: When metals are magnetized1, emulsions phase separate2, or galaxies cluster3, domain walls and patterns form and irremediably coarsen over time. This coarsening is universally driven by diffusive relaxation towards equilibrium. Here we discover a vibrational counterpart-wave coarsening-in active elastic media4-13: vibrations emerge and spontaneously grow in wavelength, period and amplitude, before a globally synchronized state called a time crystal14-17 forms. We observe wave coarsening in one- and two-dimensional mechatronic metamaterials and capture its dynamical scaling. We further arrest the process by breaking momentum conservation and reveal a far-from-equilibrium nonlinear analogue to chiral topological edge modes18-24. Our results open new questions about the transient physics of systems with non-potential interactions15,25-28 and suggest an organizing principle for nonlinear waves in acoustics29,30, optomechanics31,32, living matter6,33 and soft robotics9.

new_this_week.title: A nanosystem manipulates angiocrine signaling for cardioprotection in male mice by relocalizing endothelial exosomes
new_this_week.abstract: Acting as frontline sensors during cardiovascular injury, endothelial cells respond to acute ischemia by releasing exosomes as angiocrine signals for intercellular communication and cardioprotection. However, these endogenous signals are poorly utilized because released exosomes distribute systemically and show limited exposure in injured myocardium. Here we develop a systemically administered nanosystem for relocalizing circulating endothelial exosomes towards the myocardium, increasing their local availability. The nanosystem captures circulating endothelial exosomes, mediates their transvascular relocalization and promotes delivery to cardiomyocytes in the ischemic myocardium, thereby enhancing the local availability of native angiocrine signals. In a murine model of acute cardiac ischemia using male mice, this strategy increases endothelial exosome exposure in myocardium, improves cardiomyocyte survival, and preserves cardiac function. This approach enhances the reception of native angiocrine signals at the injured myocardium, therefore converting the originally diffuse, short-lived response into a sustained, organ-specific therapeutic exposure. Acute myocardial ischemia induces the release of endothelial exosomes with cardioprotective effect. Here, the authors show that a nanosystem relocalizes circulating endothelial exosomes to ischemic myocardium, increasing local exposure and preserving cardiac function

new_this_week.title: A swing-type solid-state host–guest system enabling spontaneous adsorption–desorption cycling
new_this_week.abstract: Macrocycle-based solid-state adsorbents offer molecularly precise platforms for the selective capture of volatile organic molecules. However, regeneration of these materials commonly relies on thermal or solvent stimulation, limiting energy efficiency and the recovery of adsorbed molecules. Developing solid-state adsorption systems that enable reversible guest release under mild conditions remains challenging, particularly for structurally similar volatile molecules. Here we show a swing-type solid-state host–guest system based on a fluorinated pillar[5]arene that enables reversible adsorption–desorption cycling of volatile methylpyridines at ambient temperature without heat or solvent stimulation. Competitive binding of nonvolatile electron-deficient acceptors drives the transformation of volatile guest inclusion phases into charge-transfer phases, releasing the volatile guests and producing a visible chromic response. Re-exposure to excess volatile vapor reverses the phase transformation, with the direction and extent of switching influenced by the relative stability of the competing host–guest assemblies and further modulated by guest size and lattice accessibility. These findings highlight an appropriate degree of thermodynamic proximity between competing solid-state complexes as an important design consideration for reversible guest exchange. More broadly, this strategy provides a route to adaptive macrocycle-based adsorbents for low-energy, visually traceable adsorption–desorption processes. Solid-state host–guest complexes derived from macrocycles provide a direct pathway from molecular recognition to adaptive functional materials, but desorption typically requires thermal activation. Here, the authors report a solid-state host–guest system with a swing-type adsorption–desorption cycle without heat or solvent stimulation.

new_this_week.title: Bioinspired nanozyme-exoskeletonized yeast-derived polysaccharides for treating comorbid anxiety and depression in inflammatory bowel disease
new_this_week.abstract: Abstract Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) is a chronic condition frequently accompanied by psychological comorbidities, such as anxiety and depression. Although current treatments may alleviate some of these symptoms, the intricate pathogenesis of these comorbidities highlights an urgent need for therapeutic strategies with combined anti-inflammatory, barrier-reparative, and microbiota-modulating effects. Herein, we develop a series of nanozyme-exoskeletonized yeast-derived polysaccharides (NZEP) by integrating nanozymes with yeast-derived polysaccharides using an insect sclerotization-inspired strategy. Among them, NZEP TA-Ce , with the highest degree of nanozyme-exoskeletonization, is capable of disrupting the inflammatory vicious cycle by inhibiting MAPK and NF-κB-mediated inflammatory signaling pathways. Oral administration of NZEP TA-Ce in mice enables effective retention and accumulation in inflamed colonic regions, reverses the homeostasis imbalance of intestinal inflammation and promotes intestinal barrier repair. Furthermore, NZEP TA-Ce treatment reverses gut microbiota dysbiosis and optimizes the composition of microbial metabolites, thereby alleviating anxiety and depressive symptoms associated with IBD. This study provides a safe and promising therapeutic strategy for the management of IBD patients and their associated psychological comorbidities.

new_this_week.title: Enhancing ω-transaminase catalysis of bulky substrates guided by binding mechanism
new_this_week.abstract: Chiral amines are indispensable building blocks in pharmaceutical synthesis. (R)-3-([1,1′-biphenyl]-4-yl)-2-aminopropan-1-ol (ABP), a key chiral amine intermediate of the drug Entresto, has remained difficult to access via enzymatic asymmetric synthesis due to the inability of ω-transaminases to accommodate its bulky ketone precursor. Here, we engineer an ω-transaminase from Bacillus megaterium by integrating Funnel metadynamics, PathDetect-SOM, and path collective variables to reconstruct the free energy surface of substrate binding, pinpointing high-energy barrier regions of the binding process and the trade-off between tunnel accessibility and productive binding. Dynamic cross-correlation network analysis further identifies distal regulatory sites governing these bottleneck regions. Iterative experimental optimization yields the 13M variant, exhibiting catalytic activity 106 times that of the wild type with >99% enantiomeric excess, enabling the efficient enzymatic asymmetric synthesis of ABP. This integrated computational-experimental framework for resolving the tunnel-pocket binding trade-off offers a generalizable strategy for engineering ω-transaminases toward bulky substrates in green pharmaceutical synthesis. This study combines enhanced sampling with experiments to reveal how bulky substrates enter and bind to ω-transaminases. Distal-site engineering balanced tunnel access and binding stability, yielding 106-fold activity and >99% selectivity.

new_this_week.title: Fatty acid metabolism controls plasma membrane cholesterol accessibility via ATGL-dependent phospholipid remodeling
new_this_week.abstract: Abstract Accessible cholesterol, the pool of membrane cholesterol with high chemical activity, regulates vital processes including vertebrate development and pathogen evasion. The mechanisms that govern plasma membrane (PM) cholesterol accessibility are incompletely understood. Using a genome-wide screen we find that acetyl-CoA carboxylase alpha (ACC1) loss causes a ~10-fold increase in PM accessible cholesterol in cells and a male mouse model. We demonstrate that reduced fatty acyl-CoA levels, achieved by targeting metabolic enzymes including ACC1, fatty acid synthase (FASN) or acyl-CoA synthetases long chain (ACSL1, 3 and 4), results in the activation of adipose triacylglycerol lipase (ATGL). ATGL activation elevates polyunsaturated diacylglycerols even in triacylglycerol-deficient backgrounds, suggesting that ATGL acts independently of triacylglycerol hydrolysis. These diacylglycerol species are utilized to generate polyunsaturated phosphatidylcholine and phosphatidylethanolamine, which raises PM fluidity and cholesterol accessibility. Conversely, ATGL inhibition rigidifies the PM, reducing PM accessible cholesterol. Increased PM fluidity impairs cholesterol transport, triggering SREBP2 activation. This study reveals a surprising link between fatty acid metabolism and cholesterol homeostasis, demonstrating how ATGL-dependent lipid remodeling tunes membrane fluidity to regulate intracellular cholesterol signaling.

new_this_week.title: Global expansion of compound drought–heatwave risk
new_this_week.abstract: The increasing frequency of compound drought and heatwave (CDHW) events poses a growing threat to water security, agriculture, and ecosystems. However, the evolution, expansion, and spatial reorganization of CDHW hotspots across global land regions remain largely unexplored. Here we track more than 2500 CDHW events using a three-dimensional connected-component (CC3D) labeling approach and show that CDHWs, often treated as spatially stationary extremes, exhibit systematic displacement over time. Larger and longer-lasting events tend to travel farther and faster, expanding the spatial footprint of compound heat and moisture stress. Most contiguous events persist for 6–12 days, displace by up to ~500 km, and reach peak daily spatial extents of 2–5 × 10⁵ km². Migration is strongest in the Northern Hemisphere mid-latitudes and is predominantly eastward. We identify emerging hotspots of increasing CDHW migration potential across the European Plains, western North America, the Amazon, the West African Sahel, Central Asia, and northern Australia. These shifts are linked to evolving large-scale atmospheric circulation and are reinforced by downstream drying through reduced moisture transport and strengthened land–atmosphere coupling. Increasing CDHW migration potential over agricultural landscapes may expand exposure to compound heat and moisture stress, particularly in grazing-dependent regions vulnerable to pastureland-to-scrubland transitions. This study shows that compound drought-heatwave events exhibit systematic displacement over time, with larger and longer-lasting events tending to travel farther and faster, especially in the Northern Hemisphere mid-latitudes, with a dominant eastward direction.

new_this_week.title: Integrated multi-omics identifies distinct immune signatures with diagnostic and therapeutic implications in immune checkpoint inhibitor-induced myocarditis
new_this_week.abstract: Abstract Immune checkpoint inhibitor-associated myocarditis (ICI-myocarditis) is a rare but frequently fatal immune-related adverse event. A comprehensive understanding of the cellular and molecular determinants driving ICI-myocarditis is essential for improving diagnostic precision and developing targeted interventions. We delineate the immune landscape of ICI-myocarditis via scRNA-seq, flow cytometry, Olink proteomics, and multiplex cytokine profiling. We demonstrate that high levels of baseline ISG15⁺CD8⁺ T cells are linked to the proinflammatory features of monocytes and in vitro experiments confirm the existence of circulating ISG15⁺CD8⁺ T cells with a high potential to induce cardiomyocyte apoptosis, supporting their pathogenic potential for cardiomyocyte cytotoxicity. Notably, intercellular crosstalk between these subsets is possibly mediated via the CCL2-CCR2 axis, and its blockade attenuated ICI-induced cardiac injury in vivo. Based on the inflammatory signature in ICI-myocarditis, we develop an 8-protein custom panel with promising performance in distinguishing ICI-myocarditis from other ICIs-treated controls. JAK-STAT pathway activation promotes inflammatory programs in both ISG15⁺CD8⁺ T cells and monocytes. Furthermore, JAK-STAT inhibition ameliorates cardiac dysfunction and inflammatory infiltration while enhancing the response to anti-PD-1 therapy in mouse models. In summary, this study implicates immune-pathogenic features of ICI-myocarditis and provides a possible basis for future therapies.

new_this_week.title: Multiplexed live imaging deciphers nuclear force-driven chromatin dynamics and embryo development
new_this_week.abstract: Mechanical forces transmitted to the nucleus regulate chromatin organization and gene expression to guide cell fate transitions. However, how the forces dynamically reshape the genome in living systems remains unclear. Here, inspired by the visualization of perinuclear chromatin detachment under low tension, we develop a genetically encoded fluorescence resonance energy transfer (FRET)-based nuclear tension sensor (NuTS) that directly quantifies forces transmitted into the nucleus through LINC complex proteins SUN1/2 and their effect on chromatin reorganization. NuTS enables high spatiotemporal mapping of forces across the nuclear envelope. Combined imaging of NuTS and lamina-associated domains (LADs) reveals that force fluctuations are coupled to LADs repositioning, and that a force of approximately 6 pN on SUN2 is required to maintain perinuclear chromatin anchoring. A drop below this threshold triggers lamin A phosphorylation at Ser22, which precedes and drives perinuclear chromatin dissociation and LAD reorganization by about 10 min. LINC-complex force transmission critically regulates cell migration and is essential for embryonic notochord development in vitro and in vivo. Our study establishes a mechanochemical framework linking nuclear forces to chromatin organization and function. Here, they develop a nuclear tension sensor (NuTS) to quantify SUN2 force for perinuclear chromatin anchoring at ~6 pN. They further demonstrate that LINC-complex force transmission is critical for cell migration and zebrafish notochord development.

new_this_week.title: Orientation tomography of lanthanide-doped nanoprobes by polarization-resolved micro-spectroscopy
new_this_week.abstract: Abstract Quantifying three-dimensional (3D) orientation is critical for understanding self-assembly and collective behavior in soft matter and biological systems. Moreover, orientational analysis of anisotropic particles can characterize locally applied forces in fluids. We present a methodology for 3D orientation tomography based on polarization-resolved spectroscopy of lanthanide-doped nanorods exhibiting multiple emission dipoles, enabling 3D orientation measurements from a single viewing angle. We develop a confocal imaging setup optimized for lanthanide luminescence and a theoretical framework to extract both the local director and order parameter in nanorod assemblies. The technique achieves 0.5 μm lateral and 1 μm axial spatial resolution and is demonstrated in dense nematic liquid-crystal assemblies, resolving complex 3D topological structures, and in microfluidic flows, mapping alignment under hydrodynamic shear. This approach provides a versatile platform for quantitative studies of collective orientation, self-assembly mechanics, and alignment induced by external forces, and can be extended to other lanthanide-labeled particles and molecular probes.

new_this_week.title: Origami-inspired folded-interlocked nanofiber aerogels for thermal insulation
new_this_week.abstract: Nanofiber aerogels (NFAs) are promising thermal insulation materials for extreme environments; however, simultaneously achieving mechanical robustness, resilience, and low thermal conductivity remains a long-standing challenge in layered NFAs, where interlaminar instability often compromises structural reliability. Here we present an origami-inspired structural engineering strategy to construct folded-interlocked nanofiber aerogels. A folded-interlocked origami skeleton, integrated with a tailored interlaminar structure, introduces geometric confinement and fiber-mediated interlaminar toughening. As a result, the aerogels exhibit high compressive strength (548.02 kPa at 80% strain) and a near-zero Poisson’s ratio. Importantly, the robust interlaminar network enhances resistance to delamination, allowing the aerogels to sustain tensile deformation up to approximately 40% strain before interlaminar failure. Meanwhile, interlaminar-guided heat-flow redistribution yields a low axial thermal conductivity of 0.035 W m−1 K−1 and pronounced anisotropic thermal insulation. This work provides an architectural strategy for designing folded-interlocked NFAs for thermal protection in aerospace and other harsh environments. Chen et al. report origami-inspired folded-interlocked nanofiber aerogels that combine mechanical resilience with low axial thermal conductivity through geometric confinement and an interlaminar fibrous network.

new_this_week.title: Spontaneous ferromagnetic Fe–La geminal atoms with spin and coordination modulation for acidic oxygen reduction
new_this_week.abstract: Synergistic spin-state and local coordination engineering offers a promising strategy for enhancing the acidic oxygen reduction reaction performance of Fe–N–C electrocatalysts, yet the precise control and stabilization of active sites remain challenging. Here we report a Fe–La geminal-atom electrocatalyst (Fe1-La1/NC) with spontaneous ferromagnetic spin ordering for acidic oxygen reduction reaction. The catalyst achieves a half-wave potential of 0.92 V and a turnover frequency of 17.3e-site−1s−1, compared with commercial Pt/C (0.87 V, 9.9e-site−1s−1). A proton exchange membrane fuel cell equipped with Fe1-La1/NC cathode delivers a high current density of 56 mA cm−2 at 0.9ViR-free under H2-O2 condition, while maintaining stable operation for 100 h at 0.67 V with 86% performance retention. Operando studies and theoretical simulations reveal that La incorporation promotes a spin-polarized high-spin Fe 3 d configuration and room-temperature ferromagnetic ordering, while also regulating the local coordination/electronic structure and oxygen-intermediate adsorption. Moreover, La enables dynamic self-adaptive stabilization of Fe sites, which mitigates the conventional activity–stability trade-off. This finding provides an avenue to rationally design efficient and selective electrocatalysts. Developing robust Fe–N–C catalysts that unite activity and durability remains challenging for acidic oxygen reduction. Here, the authors report spontaneous ferromagnetic Fe–La geminal atoms that create high-spin Fe sites and a spin pinning effect for fuel-cell catalysis.

new_this_week.title: Vacancy-mediated ultrafast oxide-ion conduction in excess-oxygen Sillén oxybromides
new_this_week.abstract: Abstract Solid oxide fuel cells (SOFCs) require electrolytes with high oxide-ion conductivity at low temperatures (200–400 °C) to reduce costs. Here, we report that Bi 1.9 Te 0.1 LaO 4.05 Br exhibits oxide-ion conductivity of 0.01 S cm⁻¹ at 233 °C within the “Norby gap” in dry atmospheres. This performance exceeds that of leading proton conductors, such as BaZr 0.8 Y 0.2 O 2.9 and BaZr 0.4 Ce 0.4 Y 0.1 Yb 0.1 O 2.9 , as well as representative oxide-ion conductors, including yttria-stabilized zirconia (YSZ), LaGaO 3 -based phases (LSGM), and Bi 2 V 0.7 Sb 0.3 O 5.5 . Bi 1.9 Te 0.1 LaO 4.05 Br also exhibits negligible chemical expansion and high chemical stability under oxidizing, reducing, and CO 2 -containing atmospheres. The high conductivity is associated with a layered Sillén structure composed of Bi-containing triple fluorite-like slabs and Br layers, together with oxygen vacancies that enable vacancy-mediated oxide-ion migration. Despite the presence of excess oxide ions, oxide-ion transport predominantly occurs via a vacancy mechanism, as revealed by ab initio molecular dynamics simulations, static density functional theory calculations, and neutron diffraction analyses. These findings establish a design principle for high-performance oxide-ion conductors based on vacancy-mediated oxide-ion transport in excess-oxygen Bi-containing Sillén oxyhalides.

new_this_week.title: The Synthetic Imputation Approach: Using LLMs to Generate Synthetic Texts for Underrepresented Categories in Supervised Classification Tasks
new_this_week.abstract: Abstract Annotated text data are central to many empirical applications in political science, yet many annotation tasks involve categories that are sparsely populated. These low- N categories pose problems for both encoder-only and decoder-only (generative) Transformer large language models (LLMs), leading to low performance, biased evaluation and measurement error in downstream analyses. This article introduces the synthetic imputation approach, a targeted method for expanding sparse categories while remaining consistent with the category-defining content of the human-coded examples. The approach uses a generative LLM to produce additional texts for underrepresented categories by conditioning on small, rotating subsets of human-coded examples. Rather than paraphrasing or replacing the original data, synthetic imputation adds informative variation only where data are thin. I evaluate the approach using both encoder-only and decoder-only LLM classifiers across multiple political science applications. The results show that synthetic imputation substantially improves performance and evaluation stability in sparse settings, recovering full-sample performance once a modest number of true observations is available, with limited and predictable overfitting at very low levels of N .
affiliations: Purdue University
new_this_week.semantic_scholar_tldr: The results show that synthetic imputation substantially improves performance and evaluation stability in sparse settings, recovering full-sample performance once a modest number of true observations is available, with limited and predictable overfitting at very low levels of N .

new_this_week.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
new_this_week.title: Autoimmunity induced by epigenome alteration affecting thymic Treg cell development
new_this_week.abstract: Methyl-CpG-binding domain protein 3 (MBD3), an essential component of the nucleosome remodeling and deacetylase (NuRD) complex, controls chromatin accessibility at lineage-specific transcriptional enhancers and promoters during hematopoietic cell differentiation. Here, we have shown that MBD3 deficiency in the T cell compartment resulted in spontaneous development of T cell–mediated multiorgan autoimmune diseases including fatal autoimmune myocarditis. The MBD3-deficient mice notably showed a significant reduction of CD25 + Foxp3 + regulatory T (Treg) cells in both the thymus and periphery without much affecting the development and function of conventional T (Tconv) cells. Mixed bone marrow (BM) chimeras reconstituted with wild-type and MBD3-deficient BM revealed a cell-intrinsic defect in thymic Treg cell lineage differentiation in MBD3-deficient cells. Transcriptional, phenotypic, and functional analyses of thymocyte subsets further revealed that MBD3 deficiency particularly affected the activation of a Treg-specific enhancer of the Il2ra gene encoding CD25, hence impaired CD25 expression in immature CD4 single-positive thymocytes (ImCD4SP) but not in peripheral T cells. The impairment markedly limited thymic Treg precursor cell generation and substantially reduced overall thymic Treg cell output. By contrast, MBD3 deficiency scarcely impacted the TGF-β/IL-2-dependent in vitro Treg cell generation from Tconv cells. Thus, Treg-specific developmental properties such as high IL-2/CD25 dependency of their thymic differentiation may render them more sensitive than Tconv cells to epigenetic changes of the whole T cell compartment. The results provide a mechanistic basis by which general epigenomic alterations in the T cell compartment can be causative of autoimmune and other immunological diseases through selectively affecting thymic Treg cell development.
affiliations: Department of Experimental Immunology, Immunology Frontier Research Center, University of Osaka
Department of Experimental Pathology, Institute for Frontier Life and Medical Sciences, Kyoto University
new_this_week.semantic_scholar_tldr: It is shown that MBD3 deficiency in the T cell compartment resulted in spontaneous development of T cell-mediated multiorgan autoimmune diseases including fatal autoimmune myocarditis and the results provide a mechanistic basis by which general epigenomic alterations in the T cell compartment can be causative of autoimmune and other immunological diseases through selectively affecting thymic Treg cell development.

new_this_week.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
new_this_week.title: Shading enhances Se accumulation in tea leaves through promoting CsMYB7-like-mediated conversion of Se (VI) to Se (IV)
new_this_week.abstract: Limited selenium (Se) accumulation in agricultural products contributes to widespread dietary Se deficiency, posing a global nutritional threat. Efficient agronomic strategies to enhance Se biofortification in crops are still lacking. Here, we reveal the synergistic effects of shading and Se nanoparticles application on Se biofortification in tea leaves. Field experiments demonstrate that shading enhances Se accumulation in tea leaves under sufficient Se supply, through activating Se metabolism pathway. We identify CsAPR1 functions at the early stage of Se assimilation, catalyzing the reduction of Se (VI). The transcription of CsAPR1 is activated by CsMYB7-like and is further promoted by shading through interaction with CsbHLH70. Under sunlight, CsHY5 competes with CsbHLH70 for binding to CsMYB7-like, thereby attenuating CsMYB7-like-mediated transcription of CsAPR1 and suppressing Se accumulation in tea plants. Our findings reveal the molecular mechanisms underlying shade-induced enhancement of Se biofortification, offering insights and strategies for Se-enriched crop production.
affiliations: Zhejiang Key Laboratory of Horticultural Crop Quality Improvement, Tea Research Institute, Zhejiang University

new_this_week.title: Public Service Decline and Support for the Populist Right: Evidence from England’s National Health Service
new_this_week.abstract: The rise of populist right parties is well studied, but relatively little attention has been given to how public service performance influences voter support. Given that public services are often the primary means through which citizens interact with the state, we argue that declining public services can create grievances that increase the appeal of populist right parties. Focusing on England’s National Health Service, we combine administrative data on local health facility closures with panel data on public preferences and voting intentions. Using a staggered difference-in-differences design, we find that closures reduce satisfaction with public services and increase support for populist right parties. These effects are moderated by migrant registrations at local health practices, highlighting the interaction between public service performance and immigration concerns in fueling populist right support. Our findings underscore the role of public service decline as a driver of support for populist parties, especially in areas undergoing demographic change.
affiliations: IE University
London School of Economics and Political Science
University of Oxford

new_this_week.title: Colossal visible birefringence and ultraviolet hyperbolicity in wide bandgap semiconductor CuAlO2
new_this_week.abstract: Materials combining colossal birefringence with a wide bandgap are of considerable interest for miniaturized photonics, yet remain rare because strong optical transitions that enhance birefringence usually introduce optical loss. Here we show that CuAlO2 exhibits colossal ultraviolet–visible birefringence alongside a wide bandgap. Spectroscopic ellipsometry on millimeter-sized single crystals reveals a sharp, intense lowest-energy transition near 3.78 eV exclusively in the ab-plane, yielding a maximum birefringence ∣Δn∣max = 3.67, and ∣Δn∣ > 0.5 throughout the visible range, with a direct band gap of 3.71 eV. The same transition generates a Type-II hyperbolic window between two ultraviolet epsilon-near-zero points. First-principles calculations and optical selection rules attribute this anisotropy to Cu-dominated band-edge states and a dipole-allowed Cu dz2-to-px/y transition enabled by the linear O–Cu–O dumbbell structure. These results establish CuAlO2 as a natural oxide platform that bridges broadband low-loss birefringence and ultraviolet hyperbolic photonics. Materials combining large optical anisotropy with a wide band gap are desirable for broadband anisotropic photonics. Here, the authors show for CuAlO2 a colossal ultraviolet–visible optical anisotropy with a maximum birefringence of 3.67 alongside a wide direct band gap of 3.71 eV.

new_this_week.title: Current aviation roadmaps are not within planetary boundaries
new_this_week.abstract: Abstract Aviation decarbonization roadmaps predominantly rely on replacing fossil kerosene with alternative jet fuels, yet the systemic impact of these alternatives on planetary boundaries other than climate change has not been quantified. Here we integrate prospective life-cycle inventories with the planetary boundaries framework to evaluate the absolute impacts of aviation roadmaps as time-dependent trajectories, rather than endpoint snapshots. Across scenarios to 2050, we find that fuel-switch-centered roadmaps do not achieve sustainability, persistently transgress the climate change and biosphere integrity core boundaries, and exert large demands for energy, land, freshwater and CO 2 capture that challenge their feasibility. Slower traffic growth brings aviation closer to its share of the safe operating space in terms of lowering energy demand, but respecting additional planetary boundaries requires air traffic to decline by at least 7.2% yr −1 . Our results show that aligning aviation with Earth’s safe operating space cannot be achieved through fuel substitution alone and requires governance strategies that combine supply-side solutions with explicit demand-side measures.

new_this_week.title: Disrupting the NAD+/NAM metabolic ratio driven by IL-1β inflammatory response potentiates chemotherapy and chemoimmunotherapy in mice
new_this_week.abstract: Nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NAD+) replenishment sensitizes tumors to immunotherapy. However, chemotherapy-induced NAD+ metabolic reprogramming remains poorly understood. Here, we show that chemotherapy induces a macrophage-dependent IL-1β inflammatory response and NAD+ metabolic reprogramming, thereby conferring chemoresistance via CD44. Mechanistically, IL-1β-induced NAD+ salvage cooperates with the clearance of nicotinamide (NAM), the physiological inhibitor of the NAD+-consuming enzymes sirtuins, to drive CD44-mediated chemoresistance by boosting the NAD+/NAM ratio for sirtuin activation. NAM phosphoribosyltransferase (NAMPT)-mediated NAD+ salvage recycles NAD+ from NAM and further triggers serine biosynthesis, ultimately supporting NAM N-methyltransferase (NNMT)-mediated NAM clearance. Importantly, NAMPT inhibition disrupts the NAD+/NAM ratio and mitigates CD44-mediated chemoresistance and NK cell dysfunction, ultimately enhancing the efficacy of chemoimmunotherapy when combined with IL-2 across multiple preclinical models of solid tumors. Thus, our findings underscore the NAD+/NAM ratio as a metabolic therapeutic target for enhancing chemotherapy and NK cell-based chemoimmunotherapy efficacy. NAD+ metabolic pathways regulate tumor growth and sensitivity to therapeutic treatment. However, the effects of chemotherapy and chemoimmunotherapy regimens on NAD metabolism remain unclear. Here, the authors identify a macrophage-driven IL-1β inflammatory signaling that regulates the NAD + /NAM metabolic ratio to drive CD44-mediated chemoresistance and NK cell dysfunction and show that disruption of the NAD + /NAM ratio sensitises tumors to chemoimmunotherapy across multiple preclinical mouse models.

new_this_week.title: Multi-day recalibration-free electrophysiology interface based on carbon nanotube thin film dry electrodes
new_this_week.abstract: Abstract Electrophysiological signals provide crucial and reliable information for decoding behavioral and cognitive human states. However, existing electrode interfaces are susceptible to artifacts or drift over time, thereby requiring frequent machine-learning model retraining. Here we present an end-to-end design of dry electrodes based on carbon nanotube (CNT) thin films, synthesized by a roll-to-roll floating catalyst chemical vapor deposition process. By balancing structural and electrical properties, we achieved low electrode-skin impedance, high signal fidelity, minimal motion artifacts, high breathability, and biocompatibility, outperforming the gold standard wet electrodes. In a multichannel myoelectric interface demonstration, these CNT electrodes maintained stable signals and consistent task performance across 14 days using only minutes of training data and no further model retraining. To our knowledge, this is the first demonstration of a multi-day recalibration-free dry electrode system under naturalistic conditions, achieved by stable electrode–skin interface, rather than ongoing algorithmic adaptation.

new_this_week.title: NiCLIP: neuroimaging contrastive language-image pretraining model for predicting text from brain activation images
new_this_week.abstract: Predicting cognitive processes from brain activation maps remains a key challenge in neuroscience. Meta-analytic functional decoding provides an estimation of behavioral profiles associated with specific brain regions; however, existing methods fail to capture the full semantic content of the neuroimaging literature. To address this, we present NiCLIP, a contrastive language-image model trained on over 23,000 articles to predict cognitive tasks, concepts, and domains from brain activation patterns. NiCLIP achieves optimal performance when using full-text articles and a curated cognitive ontology with precise task-concept-domain mappings. Our results show that NiCLIP accurately predicts cognitive tasks from Human Connectome Project group-level maps across multiple domains (e.g., emotion, language, motor) and precisely characterizes the functional roles of specific brain regions, including the amygdala, hippocampus, and temporoparietal junction. However, NiCLIP showed limitations with noisy subject-level activation maps. NiCLIP represents a significant advancement in functional decoding, offering a powerful tool for hypothesis generation and scientific discovery. Researchers developed NiCLIP, an AI model that decodes cognitive tasks, concepts, and domains from brain activation patterns. Trained on over 23,000 papers, NiCLIP excels at group-level decoding, outperforming traditional decoders.

new_this_week.title: Unmet care needs at the end-of-life among older adults with activity limitations
new_this_week.abstract: Despite the growing global demand for end-of-life care resulting from rapid social transformations, significant gaps exist in cross-national research examining unmet end-of-life care needs. Using harmonized end-of-life survey data (2010-2021) from the United States, 28 European countries, South Korea, China, and Mexico, here we show that the United States, Europe, and South Korea exhibit higher overall unmet end-of-life care needs than China and Mexico, where limited formal care provision is compensated with high levels of informal care. Death at institutions is associated with lower overall unmet end-of-life care needs in the United States and South Korea, with Mexico presenting an exception. Similarly, urban areas in Europe and South Korea exhibit lower unmet formal end-of-life care needs compared to rural areas. Among married individuals, only Mexico exhibits significantly lower unmet overall end-of-life care needs compared to unmarried individuals. Having children is consistently linked to lower unmet informal end-of-life care needs across the United States, Europe, and South Korea. Our findings highlight the complex interplay between care systems and family demographic structures in shaping end-of-life care access, and underscore the need for tailored policy approaches that strengthen both formal and informal care systems while addressing sociodemographic disparities in care access. Formal end-of-life care expansion in the US, Europe, and South Korea has not fully compensated for declining informal care, resulting in care gaps. Demographic transitions interact with development contexts to create distinct care landscapes.

new_this_week.title: Wireless, optoelectronic, multimodal skin sensor for simultaneous monitoring of mechanical stress and vascular responses
new_this_week.abstract: Prolonged mechanical loading and subsequent vascular ischemia drive the development of severe pressure injuries. Effective prevention of irreversible tissue damage requires monitoring both multiaxial mechanical forces and physiological erythema. However, conventional diagnostic tools remain limited by rigid architectures, single parameter detection, and subjective visual assessments. Here, a wireless, battery free optoelectronic multimodal sensor platform provides an integrated framework for tracking posture dependent mechanical loading and localized erythema. The soft, skin conformable device uses geometric light modulation within an isolated optical cavity to quantify normal pressure and biaxial shear stresses. To resolve complex mechanical environments, a deep neural network regression model decouples simultaneous tri-axial forces, Fx, Fy, and Fz, at the skin interface. Concurrently, a dual wavelength optical reflectance mechanism quantifies skin erythema by capturing subtle variations in hemoglobin absorption. Opaque elastomeric encapsulation shields the internal optics, supporting stable optical measurements under varying ambient illumination and skin conditions. System level integration via near field communication enables untethered operation across a multiplexed sensor network. On-body evaluations in a simulated clinical bed setting demonstrate the ability of the platform to dynamically map posture-dependent biomechanical loading and localized vascular responses, providing a technological basis for future studies on data-driven monitoring of the mechanical and vascular factors associated with pressure-injury risk. Pressure injuries arise from sustained mechanical loading and reduced blood flow, but current tools cannot objectively track both together. Cho et al. built a soft, wireless, battery-free, optoelectronic sensor that simultaneously maps three-axis stress and redness on the body.

new_this_week.title: An international multicenter study of MASLD prevalence among children and adolescents assessed by VCTE
new_this_week.abstract: The worldwide prevalence of pediatric metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) remains uncertain. Using vibration-controlled transient elastography (VCTE), we estimate the prevalence of MASLD among children and adolescents in community and hospital populations and conduct additional analyses of hepatic steatosis and fibrosis severity grades. In this international multicenter study, we include 9352 children and adolescents aged 6–18 years from 38 centers across 17 countries on five continents. In the overall population, the median age is 12.0 years (IQR: 8.5–15.1), and 5471 (58.5%) are male. The prevalence of MASLD is 17.60% (95% CI: 16.63–18.61) in the community population and 58.03% (95% CI: 56.34–59.70) in the hospital population, with corresponding age-standardized prevalences of 20.97% and 52.34%, respectively. The prevalence of MASLD in the community population is highest in South America (47.92%), followed by North America (25.05%) and Asia (13.96%). MASLD prevalence among adolescents is significantly higher in 2021–2024 compared to 2017–2020, except among those with normal weight or below. Older age, obesity, and elevated serum aminotransferase levels are independently associated with hepatic steatosis and fibrosis, whereas steatosis (grades S2 and S3) is independently associated with greater hepatic fibrosis. Our findings provide useful contemporary data for estimating the epidemiology of pediatric MASLD across diverse populations. A multicenter study in 17 countries on pediatric MASLD, a liver disorder, finds a prevalence of 18% in community populations and 58% in hospital populations, differences between regions, associations with obesity and elevated liver enzyme levels.

new_this_week.title: Anomalous spin–lattice coupling in a 2D antiferromagnetic semiconductor revealed by surface acoustic Rayleigh waves
new_this_week.abstract: Abstract Magnetic order in van der Waals magnets can strongly influence their lattice dynamics, yet how it affects local and macroscopic manifestations of spin-phonon coupling remains unclear. Optical phonons probe bond-scale exchange modulation and short-range spin correlations, whereas long-wavelength acoustic modes couple to uniform strain fields and are sensitive to renormalization of the macroscopic elastic tensor associated with long-range magnetic order. Experimentally accessing these acoustic excitations in low-dimensional crystals is challenging due to their low energies and the small lateral dimensions of exfoliated samples. Here, we employ Brillouin–Mandelstam scattering spectroscopy to investigate surface acoustic phonons in exfoliated NiPS 3 thin films across the antiferromagnetic transition. Our results show a single Rayleigh surface mode whose phase velocity decreases significantly across the Néel temperature. This anomaly reflects a strong magnetoelastic renormalization of the elastic constants triggered by the onset of antiferromagnetic order. First-principles calculations, combined with continuum finite-element modeling reproduce the Rayleigh-wave dispersion and its magnetic-order–induced shift. The results reveal how microscopic exchange interactions govern the macroscopic elastic response of two-dimensional antiferromagnetic semiconductors, enabling magnetically tunable phononic, magnonic, and strain-mediated spintronic devices.

new_this_week.title: Block-fitness modeling of the global air mobility network
new_this_week.abstract: Abstract Accurate representations of origin-destination (OD) passenger flows on the World Air Transportation Network (WAN) are fundamental inputs to models of global mobility, epidemic risk, and infrastructure planning. However, OD data are largely commercial and proprietary, therefore often inaccessible to the research community. Here we introduce a generative model that treats air mobility as a stochastic process within a sparse maximum-entropy framework, informed by aggregate traffic volumes of individual locations and geographic regions. The model accurately reconstructs both network structure and mobility flows, yielding epidemic spreading trajectories that closely match those obtained using real mobility data. Furthermore, the method can be effectively implemented using open data on flight routes and airport traffic, reducing dependence on proprietary datasets. Our approach provides a scalable, interpretable, and computationally efficient framework for scenario analysis and policy design in global mobility systems.

new_this_week.title: C-terminal evolutionary remodelling of isoleucyl-tRNA synthetases is a prokaryote-specific strategy for tuning aminoacylation rate
new_this_week.abstract: Abstract Aminoacyl-tRNA synthetases are the guardians of translational fidelity. Their complex function is mirrored by an elaborate structure, which includes multiple nested domains. While the evolutionary pressures that promoted the emergence of some domains, such as the editing domain, are clear, the pressures acting on other domains, particularly those at the C-terminus, are not. Here, we combine kinetic analysis, X-ray crystallography, and bioinformatics to unveil the history and evolutionary forces that have shaped isoleucyl-tRNA synthetase (IleRS) domain structure. We find that the traditional classification of IleRSs based on the C-terminal tRNA-recognition domains is incomplete, as it fails to capture features of the synthetic domain. Guided by a crystal structure of the Priestia megaterium IleRS2:tRNA Ile complex, we removed key interactions between IleRS2 and its cognate tRNA and characterised their impact on enzyme activity. We found that D-loop interactions with the IleRS2 C-terminal domains are non-essential in prokaryotes, and their loss can even increase catalytic turnover. Further, we show that the zinc-binding domain of IleRS1 recognises the anticodon less stringently than the canonical C-terminal domain of IleRS2. Our data suggest that C-terminal evolutionary remodelling of IleRSs is an ongoing process with a historical precedent and is consistent with selection for faster aminoacylation rate.

new_this_week.title: Deep profiling of lysine methylation by covalent enrichment-enhanced proteomics
new_this_week.abstract: Lysine methylation is a classic posttranslational modification, yet most studies focus on histone methylation. Although emerging evidence demonstrates the significance of nonhistone lysine methylation, current approaches that investigate individual proteins of interest are relatively low throughput. Proteomics provides an ideal strategy for comprehensively studying cellular posttranslational modifications, but current enrichment methods typically allow the identification of only a few hundred methyllysine sites because of insufficient enrichment efficiency for low-abundance methyllysine-containing tryptic peptides. Here we report a comprehensive lysine methylation profiling method based on covalent enrichment-enhanced quantitative proteomics, termed DEKmeP. In practice, DEKmeP enables systematic nomination of candidate substrates and their monomethylation sites regulated by lysine methyltransferases. Through subsequent biochemical and cellular experiments, we validate dozens of nonhistone substrates of lysine methyltransferases. Moreover, we characterize the functional effects of SMYD2-mediated c-Jun K288 methylation. Therefore, DEKmeP may shift lysine methylation studies from the investigation of individual proteins of interest to systematic exploration of the methyllysine proteome, thereby expanding the understanding of lysine methyltransferase catalysis and nonhistone lysine methylation. The authors report DEKmeP, a covalent enrichment-based quantitative proteomics workflow for deep lysine methylation profiling enabling systematic nomination of methyltransferase-regulated sites.

new_this_week.title: Genomic bases of short-term evolution in wild barn owls revealed by long-term monitoring and population-scale sequencing
new_this_week.abstract: Abstract Understanding how wild populations undergo rapid phenotypic evolution requires linking phenotypic change to its underlying genomic architecture over contemporary timescales. Here, we leverage a 30-year study of Swiss barn owls ( Tyto alba ) to examine long-term changes in two melanin-based traits (plumage coloration and spottiness) that have previously been linked to multiple fitness-related traits. We document a consistent temporal shift toward darker and more heavily spotted individuals and show, using whole-genome sequencing of 3,102 individuals, that these traits are controlled by a small number of loci of major effect with partially overlapping architectures. Temporal allele frequency analyses reveal subtle but consistent changes at these loci. By comparing empirical trajectories to simulations, we show that genetic drift alone is insufficient to explain the observed patterns at one major locus, indicating a role for selection. Our results demonstrate how selection acting on a small number of loci can contribute to rapid phenotypic evolution of continuous traits in the wild and highlight the value of long-term genomic and phenotypic monitoring for disentangling evolutionary processes.

new_this_week.title: Global rise of a wheat pathogen through two-stage evolutionary emergence coupled with aerial dispersal
new_this_week.abstract: The rise of plant pathogens following crop domestication and their subsequent global spread pose persistent threats to food security, yet the mechanisms underlying host jumps and rapid adaptation in obligate biotrophs remain unclear. Using 319 Puccinia striiformis f. sp. tritici (Pst) genomes and virulence phenotypes of 234 isolates across six continents, we construct its origin and global dissemination. Our analyses support a two-stage emergence model: P. striiformis sensu stricto originated and diversified in the Himalayan region, subsequently a P. striiformis s. str. lineage jumped to domesticated wheat in the Fertile Crescent, giving rise to epidemic lineage (Pst) and spreading worldwide with wheat cultivation. This host jump triggered demographic expansion and selective sweeps, while GWAS identified region-specific virulence loci shaped by resistant cultivars. Overlay of air trajectory and dispersal simulations identified atmospheric corridors consistent with genomic migration patterns, supporting a historical role for long-distance aerial transport in the pathogen’s global spread. Puccinia striiformis f. sp. tritici, an obligate fungal pathogen, threatens wheat production worldwide. Using 319 genomes and virulence data from 234 isolates globally, this study constructs its two-stage emergence and global dissemination, supporting a historical role for long-distance aerial transport.

new_this_week.title: IL-4 exploits TNF signaling to shape its gene expression signature in monocytes and macrophages
new_this_week.abstract: Investigation of crosstalk between antagonistic pro- and anti-inflammatory cytokines has focused on mechanisms and functional consequences of cross-inhibition. Here, we investigate cross-regulation between proinflammatory tumor necrosis factor (TNF) and anti-inflammatory interleukin-4 (IL-4) in primary human monocytes and in a skin wound-healing model. Surprisingly, TNF functioned mainly as a costimulator of IL-4-induced gene expression, whereas IL-4 selectively inhibited the TNF-induced IFN response, leaving inflammatory gene expression mostly intact. TNF and IL-4 synergistically induced gene sets that are important in the regulation of inflammation and tissue repair, which were highly induced during the phase of wound healing when these cytokines are co-expressed. Crosstalk between TNF and IL-4 was mediated by epigenetic chromatin-mediated mechanisms associated with cooperation between NF-κB and STAT6 transcription factors, erasure of negative histone mark H3K27me3, and selective inhibition of IRF1. These results identify a mechanism for expansion of the IL-4 response and highlight the complexity of crosstalk between antagonistic cytokines, including cooperation for select gene responses that are important for immune responses and tissue repair. Transcriptional and epigenetic mechanisms regulate responses to cytokines, as well as the crosstalk between pro- and anti-inflammatory cytokines. Here, the authors demonstrate that pro-inflammatory TNF amplifies, rather than blocks, the anti-inflammatory IL-4 response in human monocytes and that NF-κB and STAT6 cooperate on chromatin to activate tissue-repair genes.

new_this_week.title: Interpretable AI-guided discovery of degradable ionizable lipids with enhanced hepatic mRNA delivery in vivo
new_this_week.abstract: Abstract Lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) enable RNA medicines, yet ionizable-lipid discovery remains largely empirical, particularly when in vitro activity must be translated into functional hepatic delivery in vivo. Here we establish an interpretable discovery framework that combines modular degradable lipid chemistry, high-throughput phenotyping, machine learning, virtual library expansion, and independent in vivo validation to define a learnable ionizable-lipid design space. Starting from a 520-member library, we train an XGBoost model on firefly luciferase (Fluc) expression in HeLa cells and use physicochemical descriptors and molecular fingerprints to prospectively prioritize candidates with higher predicted in vitro transfection activity across a 10,920-member virtual space. In vivo phenotyping subsequently identifies PA97MD101 as a lead ionizable lipid. In mice, PA97MD101 enhances hepatic mRNA expression and Cre-dependent recombination and supports Cas9/sgTtr-mediated TTR suppression. Its performance is associated with pH-dependent membrane activity and reduced lysosomal colocalization. These findings support further evaluation of PA97MD101 for functional hepatic RNA delivery.

new_this_week.title: KMT2B facilitates long-range gene regulation through LINE1 elements
new_this_week.abstract: Transcriptional regulation is tightly linked to chromatin organization, with H3K4me3 marking active and bivalent promoters. In embryonic stem cells, KMT2B deposits H3K4me3 at bivalent promoters, yet loss of H3K4me3 at these sites leaves developmental gene transcription largely unaltered. Here, we show that, in both mouse embryonic stem cells and during differentiation, the primary role of KMT2B is not to counteract Polycomb-mediated repression at bivalent promoters. Instead, we uncover a distinct regulatory function for KMT2B at the CG-rich 5’UTR of young LINE-1 elements. KMT2B binds LINE-1 5’UTRs and maintains their active chromatin state (H3K4me3, H3K27ac, H4K16ac) while preventing repressive H3K9me3 accumulation. Using complementary genomic methods and targeted deletions, we show that KMT2B-bound LINE-1 elements act as enhancers modulating neighboring gene expression in embryonic stem cells and, particularly, during differentiation. Our findings define KMT2B regulatory functions at LINE-1 repeats and highlight transposable elements as key components of long-range gene expression control. The authors demonstrate that KMT2B primarily regulates gene expression through LINE-1 elements with enhancer-like function, rather than by counteracting Polycomb repression, revealing an underappreciated link between Trithorax proteins and transposable elements during cell differentiation.

new_this_week.title: Metabolite-mediated reversal of motor hyperactivity restores ciliary function
new_this_week.abstract: Hyperactive missense mutations can produce phenotypes that are difficult to predict from sequence alone. Here, we dissect such a discrepancy in Caenorhabditis elegans, where the kinesin mutant osm-3(A340V) shortens sensory cilia despite exhibiting elevated in vitro motility. A forward genetic screen identified osm-7, a hypodermal secreted protein, whose loss restored ciliary architecture by elevating intracellular glycerol over 100-fold. Glycerol supplementation alone recapitulated this rescue, re-establishing intraflagellar transport in neurons and modulating OSM-3(A340V) motility in vitro. Molecular dynamics simulations suggest that A340V restricts neck-helix relaxation, a defect reversed by glycerol-induced conformational tuning. Our study indicates that impairment of neck-helix flexibility leads to kinesin hyperactivity in vitro and motility defects in vivo, and that metabolite-mediated conformational tuning represents a mechanism for reversing such motor defects. A hyperactive kinesin mutation that shortens cilia is rescued by glycerol, which restores motor coordination and ciliary transport through conformational tuning, revealing a mechanism for correcting hyperactivity defects.

new_this_week.title: Neuronal signatures of successful one-shot memory in mid-level visual cortex
new_this_week.abstract: High-capacity, one-shot visual recognition memory challenges theories of learning and neural coding because it requires rapid, robust, and durable representations. Most studies have focused on the hippocampus and other higher areas. However, behavioral evidence demonstrating links between image properties and memorability and revealing image specificity of visual memory suggests an important role for mid-level visual cortex. We tested the hypothesis that area V4 contains signals critical for recognition memory in two male rhesus macaques. Our task increased difficulty, allowing comparisons of neuronal population responses on correct and error trials. We observed signatures of several proposed memory mechanisms including magnitude coding, repetition suppression, sparse coding, and population response consistency, but only sparse coding and population response consistency predicted behavior. Familiar images also evoked faster dynamics, consistent with pattern completion. These findings demonstrate that fast, high-capacity memory is supported by neural codes in mid-level sensory cortex independent of stimulus features per se, highlighting its role in distributed memory networks. Neural mechanisms underlying one-shot memory are not fully understood. In this study, macaque monkeys were trained to perform a continuous image recognition task and simultaneously recorded from groups of neurons in area V4. The authors found that the perceptual building blocks of fast, high-capacity memory are present in mid-level sensory cortex.

new_this_week.title: Precision functional mapping of imagined and experienced pain
new_this_week.abstract: Abstract Imagination is a principal human capacity, enabling simulation of sensations and situations for planning, learning, and empathy. We examined neural representations of experienced and imagined pain across eight body sites using deep-phenotyping, precision functional MRI with over seven hours of scanning per participant (N = 9). Here we show, using conventional mapping, pattern classification, and representational similarity analyses, that both imagined and experienced pain activated nociceptive regions (e.g., dorsoposterior insula) and non-nociceptive regions (e.g., premotor areas and inferior inter-effector motor cortex). However, imagined pain did not reliably reactivate body site-selective nociceptive patterns in any region. Instead, imagined and experienced pain shared multivariate representations across widespread cortical and subcortical regions, particularly transmodal cortical areas including dorsomedial and lateral prefrontal cortex, hippocampus, and thalamus. These findings suggest that imagination generates distributed pain-like activity, but with separable neural codes for imagined and experienced pain. This distinction may explain the difficulty of vividly imagining pain and clarify its potential roles in empathy, planning, and pain chronification.

new_this_week.title: Syndecan-3 couples tumor mechanics to immunosuppressive macrophage identity
new_this_week.abstract: Tumor-associated macrophages adopt suppressive states, but how tumor stress installs these programs remains unclear. Here, we identify syndecan-3 (SDC3) as a macrophage-intrinsic mechanosensory regulator by integrating in vivo functional screening, single-cell and spatial profiling, and genetic and pharmacological perturbation. SDC3+ macrophages accumulate in hypoxic, stiff tumor niches and suppress antitumor cytotoxic T-cell responses. Matrix stiffness increases mechanical loading on SDC3, reorganizes an SDC3-associated scaffold and opens suppressive chromatin loci. This program engages a CDK7–MAFB relay to induce TREM2, which functions as a required suppressive effector in mice. Human-cell assays support a species-specific TREM2-associated inhibition mechanism. Naldemedine engages TREM2, restores cytotoxic T-cell activity, improves tumor control and enhances immune-checkpoint blockade in vivo. These findings define a targetable SDC3–CDK7–MAFB–TREM2 axis linking hypoxia and tissue mechanics to macrophage-mediated immune evasion. Tumor associated macrophages (TAMs) are a main component of the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (TME). Here the authors identify syndecan-3 as a macrophage-intrinsic mechano-sensor that drives immunosuppression in the TME.

new_this_week.title: Targeting MDA5 induces immunogenic cell death and promotes anti-tumor immunity
new_this_week.abstract: Identifying targets to enhance tumor immunity is an urgent need. Although nucleic acid sensors play critical roles in promoting tumor immune clearance, their exceptionally low mutation rate in cancers suggests potential unexplored roles in tumor progression. Here, we demonstrate that the RNA sensor melanoma differentiation-associated protein 5 (MDA5) promotes immune evasion, and its high expression is strongly predictive of poor survival and resistance to immune checkpoint blockade (ICB) therapy in patients. Targeting MDA5 reshapes the tumor microenvironment, strengthening immune memory responses and enhancing effector CD8⁺ T cell activity in preclinical models in female mice. Mechanistically, MDA5 deficiency triggers unfolded protein response driven immunogenic cell death through induction of damage-associated molecular patterns, leading to enhanced dendritic cell-mediated antigen engulfment and T cell activation. Additionally, MDA5 loss primes the ASK1-JNK/P38 signaling pathway, sensitizing tumor cells to TNF-α/IFN-γ, further amplifying this process. Consequently, targeting MDA5 enhances the efficacy of ICB therapy across multiple cancer types, positioning it as a promising therapeutic target. RNA sensors have been linked to antitumor immune responses. Here, based on results of in vivo CRISPR screens, the authors propose the RNA sensor MDA5 as a regulator of immune evasion, showing that its targeting induces immunogenic cell death and anti tumor immunity.

new_this_week.title: The central coupler of ClpXP controls intersubunit communication and couples intrasubunit chemical energy with force generation
new_this_week.abstract: Abstract ClpX is a clockwise hexameric helical arrangement that hydrolyzes ATP to unfold proteins and translocate them into the proteolytic chamber. We investigate the central coupler, a three α-helix module conserved among AAA+ ATPases, which is proposed to enable intersubunit communication and mechanochemical coupling. Although fundamental in AAA+ ATPases, the molecular mechanism underlying these processes remains elusive in ClpX. By combining single-molecule optical tweezers, biochemical assays and single-particle cryo-EM we demonstrate that the central coupler, of the second-highest subunit of the ClpX clockwise helical arrangement, positions its Arginine-finger, sensor-I and sensor-II to contact the ATP of the anticlockwise neighbor subunit to trigger its hydrolysis. Then, the central coupler of the highest subunit rapidly couples the ATP hydrolysis with the downward motion of its substrate-translocating loop, enabling fast force generation to swiftly unfold protein substrates while maximizing the thermodynamic efficiency of the motor.

new_this_week.title: Less can be more for predicting properties with large language models
new_this_week.abstract: Abstract Predicting properties from coordinate–category data—sets of vectors paired with categorical information—is fundamental to computational science, manifesting in materials science as predicting formation energies or elastic moduli from crystal structures. While large language models (LLMs) have increasingly been applied to such tasks, optimal strategies for achieving reliable predictions remain elusive. Here we report fundamental limitations in LLM’s ability to learn from coordinate information in coordinate–category data. Through systematic experiments using synthetic datasets with tunable coordinate and category contributions, and a comprehensive benchmarking framework (MatText), we find that LLMs consistently fail to capture coordinate information while excelling at category patterns. This geometric blindness persists regardless of model size (up to 70 billion parameters), dataset scale (up to 2 × 10 6 structures) or text representation strategy. For material property prediction tasks dominated by structural effects, specialized geometric architectures consistently outperform LLMs, as evidenced by a clear ‘Graph Neural Network Language Model (GNN-LM) wall’ in performance benchmarks. Our analysis provides concrete guidelines for architecture selection in scientific machine learning.

new_this_week.title: Simulated responses from large language models are weak proxies for human economic preferences across 74 countries
new_this_week.abstract: Large-scale surveys are central to investigating economic preferences but are costly and slow. Can large language model (LLM)-simulated responses substitute for human survey data? We conducted a virtual Global Preference Survey, simulating six experimentally validated economic preferences for 67,201 matched human respondents across 74 countries. Across 20 LLM configurations with diverse prompts and robustness checks, we found systematic but modest individual-level alignment (87.5% of Spearman correlations have 95% confidence intervals (CIs) above zero), with LLMs recovering the direction of associations in 77.8% (95% CI, (71.6%, 83.1%); CI-based consistency ratio) of gender, age and cognitive-ability dimensions, but only 48.1% (95% CI, (45.1%, 51.2%)) of cultural dimensions. Ablation and error decompositions suggest weaker alignment when removing demographic information than when removing country labels, and in many models alignment is weaker in economically undeveloped and less digitally connected countries. LLM-simulated responses may recover some individual- and group-level patterns but are not yet reliable proxies for cross-national representative surveys in macro-level inference or policy evaluation.

new_this_week.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
new_this_week.title: A Kv4.2-mGluR5 complex drives enhanced depotentiation in a mouse model of improved cognitive flexibility
new_this_week.abstract: Memory updating promotes cognitive flexibility by enabling suppression of outdated information to optimize behavioral strategies in response to a changing environment. While some circuits involved have been identified, the synaptic mechanisms underlying this process remain uncertain. Here, using a recently developed Kv4.2 knock-in mouse model (Kv4.2TA), we identify a metaplasticity in the hippocampus that accompanies an improvement in cognitive flexibility. Mutation of a C-terminal phosphorylation site (T607) in the alpha subunit of the voltage-gated K + channel protein Kv4.2 drives boosted depotentiation of spike timing-dependent long-term synaptic potentiation mediated by mGluR5 receptors, putative constituents of Kv4.2 macromolecular complexes. We found that mGluR5 receptors are required for the improved cognitive flexibility observed in Kv4.2TA mice. These findings reveal a synaptic correlate associated with memory updating in cognitive flexibility and spotlight the Kv4.2-mGluR5 complex as a therapeutic target for disorders characterized by impairments in cognitive flexibility.

new_this_week.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
new_this_week.title: AI-generated language remains systematically distinguishable from human communication
new_this_week.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used in the social sciences to simulate human behavior and communication, yet validation methods for these applications remain limited. Existing evaluations often rely on human judgments of plausibility, a coarse, difficult-to-scale, and often unreliable benchmark for distinguishing AI-generated from human text. As a result, researchers lack robust tools for assessing the realism of LLM-generated language and for calibrating models to real-world data. We address this gap in two ways. First, we introduce the Conversational Human Authenticity Test (CHAT), a validation framework that combines aggregate metrics of detectability and semantic similarity with interpretable linguistic features, including stylistic markers and topical patterns, to assess how closely LLMs approximate human language in a given dataset. Second, we benchmark nine open-weight LLMs across five calibration strategies, including fine-tuning, stylistic prompting, and context retrieval, on user interactions from X, Bluesky, and Reddit. We find that even after calibration, LLM outputs remain clearly distinguishable from human text, especially in affective tone and emotional expression. Instruction-tuned models generally underperform base models, and larger models do not obviously improve human-likeness. We also identify a trade-off between realism and semantic fidelity: methods that make outputs seem more human often move them further from the content of human responses. Together, these results provide a scalable framework for validation and calibration in LLM-based social simulation while underscoring current limits in reproducing human communication.
